work: Enarratio in Epistolam B. Pauli ad Colossenses
source: Dionysii Cartusiani Opera Omnia, t. XIII (Montreuil)

1.title: EXPOSITIO CAPITULI PRIMI : PAULUS APOSTOLUS JESU CHRISTI, ETC.
1.title_en: Exposition of the first chapter: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ, etc.

paras.t: Paulus apostolus Jesu Christi per voluntatem Dei, id est divina voluntate constitutus apostolus, et Timotheus frater: quem propter suam auctoritatem connectit sibi Apostolus: erat enim Ephesiorum episcopus. Hi itaque scribunt his qui sunt Colossis, id est in civitate sic dicta, sanctis et fidelibus fratribus, id est veraciter christianis, qui implere conantur illud Salvatoris: Estote perfecti sicut et Pater vester cælestis perfectus est; in Christo Jesu, id est in doctrina et fide Christi. Illas enim servando et operando, sancti et fideles fuerunt. Gratia gratum faciens vobis et pax, id est tranquillitas mentis, præstetur et conservetur a Deo Patre nostro, id est in cælis Patre æterno, et a Domino Jesu Christo: qui secundum divinam naturam, est causa gratiæ effectiva ac principalis. Quæcumque enim facit Pater, hæc et Filius similiter facit. Secundum humanam vero naturam, est causa gratiæ meritoria, instrumentalis ac mediata.
paras.en: [[1:1|Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ, by the will of God|Paulus apostolus Jesu Christi per voluntatem Dei]], that is, made an apostle by the divine will, [[1:1|and Timothy, a brother|et Timotheus frater]]: whom the Apostle joins to himself because of his authority, for he was bishop of the Ephesians. These, then, write to those [[1:2|who are at Colossa|qui sunt Colossis]], that is, in the city so called, [[1:2|To the saints and faithful brethren|sanctis et fidelibus fratribus]], that is, to true Christians, who strive to fulfil that saying of the Saviour: [[Matt 5:48|Be you therefore perfect, as also your heavenly Father is perfect|Estote perfecti sicut et Pater vester cælestis perfectus est]]; [[1:2|in Christ Jesus|in Christo Jesu]], that is, in the teaching and faith of Christ; for by keeping and practising these they were saints and faithful. [[1:3|Grace|Gratia]] that maketh pleasing [gratia gratum faciens: sanctifying grace, which makes the soul pleasing to God] [[1:3|be to you and peace|vobis et pax]], that is, tranquillity of mind, granted and preserved [[1:3|from God our Father|a Deo Patre nostro]], that is, from the eternal Father in heaven, [[1:3|and from the Lord Jesus Christ|et a Domino Jesu Christo]]: who according to his divine nature is the effective and principal cause of grace. For [[John 5:19|what things soever he doth, these the Son also doth in like manner|Quæcumque enim facit Pater, hæc et Filius similiter facit]]. But according to his human nature he is the meritorious, instrumental and mediate cause of grace.

paras.t: Gratias ipsius Dei et Patris Domini nostri Jesu Christi, id est Patri æterno: qui est Deus Christi, ut homo est; pater vero, secundum divinam naturam quam habet a Patre; semper, id est congruis horis, pro vobis orantes; audientes fidem vestram fundatam ac fixam in Christo Jesu, et dilectionem, id est habitum, actum interiorem, et opera caritativa, quam habetis extentam in omnes sanctos, id est universos veraciter christianos, quibus pro loco et tempore, secundum vestram possibilitatem, benefacitis, spiritualia vel corporalia beneficia impendendo, propter spem, id est beatitudinem speratam, quæ reposita, id est parata, est vobis in cælis, quam audistis, id est, quæ vobis prædicata est, in verbo veritatis, id est in vero sermone, Evangelii, quod pervenit ad vos, id est, vobis annuntiatum est, sicut et in universo mundo est, id est, cunctis gentibus evangelizatum est sicut et vobis: sic tamen, ut sit distributio, non pro singulis generum, sed pro generibus singulorum. Unde et Apostolis aiebat Salvator: Euntes in mundum universum, prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ: et Psalmista, In omnem (inquit) terram exivit sonus eorum. Et fructificat, et crescit: id est, evangelica doctrina in credentibus est cau[…]sa fructificationis et spiritualis incrementi, videlicet bonorum operum, et quotidiani profectus in gratia. Crescit quoque per hoc, quod pluribus annuntiatur, a quibus et devote recipitur. Sicut in vobis fructificavit et crevit, ex ea die qua audistis et cognovistis gratiam Dei, id est beneficia gratiæ vobis a Christo exhibita, in veritate, id est veraciter, vel in veritate evangelicæ legis;
paras.en: [[1:3|We give thanks to God and the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ|Gratias ipsius Dei et Patris Domini nostri Jesu Christi]], that is, to the eternal Father: who is the God of Christ, as Christ is man, but his Father according to the divine nature which he has from the Father; [[1:3|always|semper]], that is, at the fitting hours, [[1:3|praying|orantes]] [[1:3|for you|pro vobis]]; [[1:4|Hearing your faith|audientes fidem vestram]], founded and fixed [[1:4|in Christ Jesus|in Christo Jesu]], [[1:4|and the love|et dilectionem]], that is, the habit, the inward act, and the works of charity, [[1:4|which you have|quam habetis]], reaching out [[1:4|towards all the saints|in omnes sanctos]], that is, to all true Christians, to whom you do good as place and time allow and as far as you are able, bestowing spiritual or bodily benefits; [[1:5|For the hope|propter spem]], that is, the beatitude hoped for, [[1:5|that is laid up|quæ reposita]], that is, prepared, [[1:5|for you in heaven|est vobis in cælis]], [[1:5|which you have heard|quam audistis]], that is, which was preached to you, [[1:5|in the word of the truth|in verbo veritatis]], that is, in the true discourse, [[1:5|of the gospel|Evangelii]], [[1:6|Which is come unto you|quod pervenit ad vos]], that is, has been announced to you, [[1:6|as also it is in the whole world|sicut et in universo mundo est]], that is, it has been preached to all nations as also to you: yet so that the distribution is made not for each individual of every kind, but for every kind of individuals [a scholastic distinction: the gospel is in the whole world because it has reached men of every kind, not every single man]. Hence the Saviour said to the Apostles: [[Mark 16:15|Go ye into the whole world and preach the gospel to every creature|Euntes in mundum universum, prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ]]; and the Psalmist says: [[Ps 18:5|Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth|In omnem (inquit) terram exivit sonus eorum]]. [[1:6|and bringeth forth fruit and groweth|Et fructificat, et crescit]]: that is, the gospel teaching is in believers the cau[…]se of fruitfulness and of spiritual increase, namely of good works and of daily progress in grace. It grows also in this, that it is announced to more people, by whom it is also devoutly received. [[1:6|even as it doth in you|Sicut in vobis]] it has borne fruit and grown, [[1:6|since the day you heard and knew the grace of God|ex ea die qua audistis et cognovistis gratiam Dei]], that is, the benefits of grace shown you by Christ, [[1:6|in truth|in veritate]], that is, truly, or in the truth of the gospel law;

paras.t: sicut didicistis ab Epaphra confirmante prædicationem Archippi, carissimo conservo nostro, qui est fidelis pro vobis, id est pro vestra salute procuranda, minister Jesu Christi, ejus doctrinam vobis annuntiando, ipsumque pro vobis jugiter exorando; qui etiam manifestavit, id est, clare retulit, nobis dilectionem vestram exsistentem in spiritu, quia a Spiritu Sancto infunditur, conservatur, et secundum eum operatur; est quoque in spiritu vestro, id est in superiori parte animæ vestræ, ut in subjecto.
paras.en: [[1:7|As you learned of Epaphras|sicut didicistis ab Epaphra]], who confirmed the preaching of Archippus, [[1:7|our most beloved fellow servant|carissimo conservo nostro]], [[1:7|who is for you a faithful|qui est fidelis pro vobis]], that is, for procuring your salvation, [[1:7|minister of Christ Jesus|minister Jesu Christi]], by announcing his teaching to you and praying to him for you without ceasing; [[1:8|Who also hath manifested|qui etiam manifestavit]], that is, clearly reported, to us [[1:8|your love|dilectionem vestram]] existing [[1:8|in the spirit|in spiritu]], because it is infused and preserved by the Holy Ghost and works according to him; it is also in your spirit, that is, in the higher part of your soul, as in its subject [that is, the power of the soul in which it resides].

paras.t: Ideo et nos ex qua die audivimus tanta bona de vobis, non cessamus opportuno tempore, pro vobis orantes cordiali affectu, et postulantes prece vocali, ut impleamini agnitione voluntatis ejus, id est, divinitus copiose illustremini ad cognoscendum quid velit Deus, ut sciatis et attendatis ejus mandata atque consilia. Quid vero sit ita impleri, et quomodo fiat, subjungitur: in omni sapientia sacræ Scripturæ, id est, quam Scriptura divinitus inspirata proponit ac docet, et intellectu spirituali, id est interna, vera seu mystica intelligentia Scripturarum, quatenus litteram occidentem spiritualiter intelligatis: spiritus quippe vivificat; ut ambuletis in semitis præceptorum digne Deo, id est tam reverenter, sancte et perfecte, quam decet tanto principi deservire, atque ut eum pro præmio mereamini possidere. Maledictus enim qui facit opus Dei negligenter. Per omnia, id est in interioribus et exterioribus, placentes Domino Deo. Nam si quis totam legem impleverit, offendat autem in uno, factus est omnium reus. Cui et illud quoque Sapientis consonat: Qui in uno peccaverit, multa bona perdet. In omni opere bono fructificantes, proficiendo in meritis; et crescentes in scientia Dei, id est in notitia divinorum: de qua ait per Prophetam, Scientiam Dei volui magis quam holocausta; itidem et Sapiens, Vani sunt, inquit, omnes homines quibus non subest scientia Dei. Denique hæc est vita æterna, ut cognoscamus Deum verum.
paras.en: [[1:9|Therefore we also, from the day that we heard it|Ideo et nos ex qua die audivimus]], such good things of you, [[1:9|cease not|non cessamus]] at fitting times [[1:9|to pray for you|pro vobis orantes]] with heartfelt affection, [[1:9|and to beg|et postulantes]] with spoken prayer, [[1:9|that you may be filled with the knowledge of his will|ut impleamini agnitione voluntatis ejus]], that is, that you may be abundantly enlightened from on high to know what God wills, so that you may know and heed his commandments and counsels. What it is to be so filled, and how it comes about, is added: [[1:9|in all wisdom|in omni sapientia]] of holy Scripture, that is, the wisdom which Scripture, divinely inspired, sets forth and teaches, [[1:9|and spiritual understanding|et intellectu spirituali]], that is, the inward, true or mystical understanding of the Scriptures, so that you may understand spiritually the letter that killeth: for [[2 Cor 3:6|the spirit quickeneth|spiritus quippe vivificat]]; [[1:10|That you may walk|ut ambuletis]] in the paths of the commandments [[1:10|worthy of God|digne Deo]], that is, as reverently, holily and perfectly as it becomes us to serve so great a prince, and so that you may merit to possess him as your reward. For [[Jer 48:10|Cursed be he that doth the work of the Lord|Maledictus enim qui facit opus Dei]] negligently [the Vulgate reads "the work of the Lord deceitfully"; Denis has "the work of God negligently"]. [[1:10|in all things|Per omnia]], that is, in things inward and outward, [[1:10|pleasing|placentes]] the Lord God. For [[Jas 2:10|whosoever shall keep the whole law, but offend in one point, is become guilty of all|si quis totam legem impleverit, offendat autem in uno, factus est omnium reus]]. With which that saying of the Wise man also agrees: [[Eccles 9:18|he that shall offend in one, shall lose many good things|Qui in uno peccaverit, multa bona perdet]]. [[1:10|being fruitful in every good work|In omni opere bono fructificantes]], by advancing in merits; [[1:10|and increasing in the knowledge of God|et crescentes in scientia Dei]], that is, in the knowledge of divine things: of which he says by the Prophet: [[Osee 6:6|the knowledge of God|Scientiam Dei]] [[Osee 6:6|I desired|volui]] [[Osee 6:6|more than holocausts|magis quam holocausta]]; and likewise the Wise man: [[Wis 13:1|are vain|Vani sunt]], he says, [[Wis 13:1|all men|omnes homines]] [[Wis 13:1|in whom there is not the knowledge of God|quibus non subest scientia Dei]]. Lastly, [[John 17:3|this is eternal life: That they may know thee, the only true God|hæc est vita æterna, ut cognoscamus Deum verum]] [Denis has "that we may know the true God"].

paras.t: Possunt quoque per prædictam sapientiam, intellectum, atque scientiam, intelligi tria dona Spiritus Sancti, de quibus apud Isaiam legitur: Requiescet super eum spiritus sapientiæ et intellectus, etc. Sicque sapientia appellatur habitualis notitia supernaturalis, a Spiritu Sancto infusa ac saporosa, per quam anima sortitur rectum judicium de divinis, habendo connaturalitatem quamdam cum eis per gustum ac dilectionem. Intellectus vero est donum Spiritus Sancti per quod anima ea quæ fidei sunt penetrat, clare cognoscit, et firmiter eis inhæret, cernendo aliquam rationem propter quam assentiendum est articulis seu testimoniis fidei. Porro scientia est donum quo anima recte judicat de rebus creatis. Hæc autem prout dona sunt, non inveniuntur nisi in habentibus caritatem et gratiam, sicut nec cetera dona Spiritus Sancti. Et juxta hunc modum littera sic exponetur: In omni, id est perfecta, sapientia quæ est præstantissimum donum Spiritus Sancti, et intellectu spirituali, id est dono intellectus a Spiritu Sancto infuso.
paras.en: By the wisdom, understanding and knowledge spoken of, the three gifts of the Holy Ghost may also be understood, of which we read in Isaias: There [[Is 11:2|shall rest upon him: the spirit of wisdom, and of understanding|Requiescet super eum spiritus sapientiæ et intellectus]], etc. So wisdom is the name of a habitual supernatural knowledge, infused by the Holy Ghost and full of savour [saporosa: Denis plays on sapientia, wisdom, and sapor, taste], by which the soul obtains a right judgement of divine things, having a certain connaturality with them through taste and love. Understanding is the gift of the Holy Ghost by which the soul penetrates the things that are of faith, knows them clearly and clings to them firmly, discerning some reason for which assent must be given to the articles or testimonies of the faith. Knowledge, again, is the gift by which the soul judges rightly of created things. These, inasmuch as they are gifts, are found only in those who have charity and grace[[Wis 1:4||]], as is also true of the other gifts of the Holy Ghost. And in this way the letter will be expounded thus: [[1:9|in all|In omni]], that is, perfect, [[1:9|wisdom|sapientia]], which is the most excellent gift of the Holy Ghost, [[1:9|and spiritual understanding|et intellectu spirituali]], that is, by the gift of understanding infused by the Holy Ghost.

paras.t: In omni virtute theologica, intellectuali ac morali, confortati: optimum enim est gratia stabiliri cor; secundum potentiam claritatis ejus, id est secundum quod Deus idoneus est ad confortandum vos per claritatem gratiæ suæ; in omni patientia in adversis servata, et longanimitate, æquanimiter præstolando divina promissa, cum gaudio mentis, ex actu virtuoso manante.
paras.en: [[1:11|with all might|In omni virtute]], theological, intellectual and moral [virtus: "might" in the Douay-Rheims, but also "virtue", as Denis takes it here], [[1:11|Strengthened|confortati]]: for [[Heb 13:9|it is best that the heart be established with grace|optimum enim est gratia stabiliri cor]]; [[1:11|according to the power of his glory|secundum potentiam claritatis ejus]], that is, according as God is able to strengthen you by the brightness of his grace [claritas: "glory" in the Douay-Rheims, literally "brightness"]; [[1:11|in all patience|in omni patientia]] kept in adversity, [[1:11|and longsuffering|et longanimitate]], awaiting the divine promises with an even mind, [[1:11|with joy|cum gaudio]] of mind, flowing from the virtuous act.

paras.t: Gratias agentes Deo Patri, qui dignos nos fecit per merita Christi, gratiam baptismi et cetera opera meritoria, quæ in nobis producit, in partem, id est habendam participationem, sortis Sanctorum, id est hereditatis electorum, scilicet vitæ æternæ, quæ habetur in lumine, id est per lumen gloriæ, vel in claritate divinæ visionis. De qua sorte ait Psalmista: Dominus pars hereditatis meæ […] etiam de lumine isto testatur: In lumine tuo, inquiens, videbimus lumen. Hæc tamen hereditas dicta est sors, quia de voluntatis electione, non humana probatione distribuitur, quemadmodum sortes dicuntur temperari atque disponi a Deo.
paras.en: [[1:12|Giving thanks to God the Father|Gratias agentes Deo Patri]], [[1:12|who hath made us worthy|qui dignos nos fecit]] through the merits of Christ, the grace of baptism and the other meritorious works which he brings about in us, [[1:12|to be partakers|in partem]], that is, to have a share, [[1:12|of the lot of the saints|sortis Sanctorum]], that is, of the inheritance of the elect, namely of eternal life, which is had [[1:12|in light|in lumine]], that is, through the light of glory, or in the brightness of the divine vision. Of which lot the Psalmist says: [[Ps 15:5|The Lord is the portion of my inheritance|Dominus pars hereditatis meæ]] […] also bears witness of that light: [[Ps 35:10|in thy light|In lumine tuo]], he says, [[Ps 35:10|we shall see light|videbimus lumen]] [the margin gives Ps. xv, 10; the words are Ps 35:10]. Yet this inheritance is called a lot, because it is distributed by the choice of the will, not by human proving, just as lots are said to be ordered and disposed by God[[Prov 16:33||]].

paras.t: Qui eruit nos per incarnationem, conversationem ac passionem unigeniti sui, de potestate tenebrarum, id est a dominio dæmonum, a jugo peccati et ignorantiæ, et transtulit in regnum, id est in societatem Ecclesiæ militantis seu numerum electorum. Quæ Ecclesia dicitur regnum Christi, qui in corde fideli regnat per fidem et gratiam, quo regno aiebat angelus: Regnabit in domo Jacob in æternum: et Isaias, super solium David, et super regnum ejus sedebit. Nunc quoque translati sumus in regnum cœlorum in spe, transferendi tandem in re. Transtulit itaque nos Pater in regnum Filii dilectionis sui, qui est Filii sui dilecti, de quo ait: Hic est Filius meus dilectus, ipsum audite. […] hoc elucescit, quod dilectio in divinis non solum notionaliter seu relative, sed etiam absolute dicatur. Alias Filius a Spiritu Sancto diceretur procedere. Prædicta autem ereptione et translatione generis humani, Pater ait per Prophetam ad Filium: Dedi te in fœdus populi, in lucem gentium, ut educeres de conclusione vinctum, de domo carceris sedentes in tenebris.
paras.en: [[1:13|Who hath delivered us|Qui eruit nos]], through the incarnation, life and passion of his only-begotten, [[1:13|from the power of darkness|de potestate tenebrarum]], that is, from the dominion of the devils, from the yoke of sin and ignorance, [[1:13|and hath translated us into the kingdom|et transtulit in regnum]], that is, into the fellowship of the Church militant, or the number of the elect. This Church is called the kingdom of Christ, who reigns in the faithful heart by faith and grace; of which kingdom the angel said: [[Luke 1:32|he shall reign in the house of Jacob for ever|Regnabit in domo Jacob in æternum]]; and Isaias: [[Is 9:7|he shall sit upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom|super solium David, et super regnum ejus sedebit]]. Even now we have been translated into the kingdom of heaven in hope, to be translated at last in reality. So the Father has translated us into the kingdom [[1:13|of the Son of his love|Filii dilectionis sui]], that is, of his beloved Son, of whom he says: [[Matt 17:5|This is my beloved Son|Hic est Filius meus dilectus]], [[Matt 17:5|hear ye him|ipsum audite]]. […] this makes it plain that love in God is said not only notionally or relatively but also absolutely [that is, "love" here names the divine nature common to the three Persons, and not only the Holy Ghost, who proceeds as Love]. Otherwise the Son would be said to proceed from the Holy Ghost. Of this deliverance and translation of mankind the Father says to the Son by the Prophet: [[Is 42:6|I have given thee for a covenant of the people, for a light of the Gentiles|Dedi te in fœdus populi, in lucem gentium]], to [[Is 42:7|bring forth the prisoner out of prison, and them that sit in darkness out of the prison house|ut educeres de conclusione vinctum, de domo carceris sedentes in tenebris]].

paras.t: In quo Christo, id est per cujus sanguinis pretium, mortisque meritum, […] a peccato et […] diaboli. […] ut testatur S. Joannes in Apocalypsi: […] dilexit nos, et lavit nos a peccatis nostris in sanguine suo.
paras.en: [[1:14|In whom|In quo]], that is, in Christ, through the price of whose blood and the merit of whose death […] from sin and […] of the devil. […] as St. John testifies in the Apocalypse: […] [[Apoc 1:5|hath loved us and washed us from our sins in his own blood|dilexit nos, et lavit nos a peccatis nostris in sanguine suo]].

paras.t: Qui est imago Dei Patris invisibilis visione corporali ac intellectuali, id est omnino incomprehensibilis comprehensione perfecta, sicut et Pater. Nemo enim novit Filium nisi Pater, nec Patrem quis novit nisi Filius. In patria tamen videtur per speciem, sed non perfecte ac plene comprehenditur. Dicitur autem Christus imago Patris perfecta, non imitativa; naturalis, non artificialis; plena, non participata, id est per omnia similis Patri. Propter quod ipse ait: Qui videt me, videt et Patrem. Ad rationem autem imaginis duo requiruntur, videlicet similitudo in specie, vel saltem in signo speciei (quod maxime est figura in rebus corporeis), et processio. Oportet enim ut imago alicujus, sit ab eo cujus est imago. Filius autem in divinis generatur a Patre, in nullo distans ab eo. Dupliciter quoque dicitur esse imago alicujus in alio. Primo, sicut in re ejusdem naturæ, saltem secundum speciem, sicut imago regis est in filio ejus. Et ita Filius Dei vocatur imago Patris. Secundo, tanquam in re alterius generis, sicut imago Herculis est in lapide, et imago imperatoris in nummo. Sicque vocatur homo imago Dei, qui potius dicendus est factus ad imaginem Dei, quam ejus imago. Primogenitus omnis creaturæ, id est ante omnia creata æternaliter genitus, quemadmodum per Sapientem testatur: Ego ex ore Altissimi prodivi primogenita ante omnem creaturam.
paras.en: [[1:15|Who is the image|Qui est imago]] of God the Father, [[1:15|invisible|invisibilis]] to bodily and to intellectual sight, that is, wholly incomprehensible by perfect comprehension, as the Father also is. For [[Matt 11:27|no one knoweth the Son but the Father: neither doth any one know the Father, but the Son|Nemo enim novit Filium nisi Pater, nec Patrem quis novit nisi Filius]]. In the fatherland [that is, in heaven] he is indeed seen by sight [per speciem: in open vision, as against faith], but he is not perfectly and fully comprehended. Now Christ is called the image of the Father: perfect, not imitative; natural, not artificial; full, not participated, that is, like the Father in all things. For which reason he himself says: [[John 14:9|he that seeth me seeth the Father also|Qui videt me, videt et Patrem]]. Two things are required for an image: likeness in species, or at least in a sign of the species (which in bodily things is chiefly the shape), and procession. For the image of anything must come from that of which it is the image. And the Son in God is begotten of the Father, differing from him in nothing. An image of something is also said to be in another in two ways. First, as in a thing of the same nature, at least according to species, as the image of a king is in his son; and in this way the Son of God is called the image of the Father. Secondly, as in a thing of another kind, as the image of Hercules is in a stone, and the image of the emperor on a coin; and in this way man is called the image of God, though he should rather be said to be made to the image of God than to be his image. [[1:15|the firstborn of every creature|Primogenitus omnis creaturæ]], that is, eternally begotten before all created things, as he testifies through the Wise man: [[Ecclus 24:5|I came out of the mouth of the most High, the firstborn before all creatures|Ego ex ore Altissimi prodivi primogenita ante omnem creaturam]].

paras.t: Quia in ipso, id est per ipsum, condita sunt universa: omnia enim per ipsum facta sunt, ait Evangelista. Vel, In ipso, tanquam in exemplari principio, condita, id est creari disposita, sunt universa. Filius quippe est ars rationibus plena, omnisque creaturæ exemplar. Propter quod omnia in ipso exemplariter præexsistunt, æternaliterque a Patre præordinata atque prævisa sunt. Comparantur namque creaturæ ad ipsum, sicut artificiata ad artificem, juxta illud Sapientiæ: Omnium est […] enim artifex, omnem habens scientiam. Omnia ergo in ipso sunt condita, in cœlis et in terra, videlicet visibilia, ut corpora cœlestia, elementa passiva et mixta, et invisibilia, de quibus adjectum est: sive Throni, id est angeli de infimo choro primæ et summæ hierarchiæ angelicæ. Qui Throni, id est sedes, vocantur, quoniam propter magnam suam propinquitatem ad Deum, ipse in eis sedere, quiescere, præsidere, et per eos sua judicia exercere asseritur. Sive Dominationes, sive Principatus, sive Potestates. Hos tres ordines angelorum nominavit Apostolus ad Ephesios: de quibus ibi satis dictum videtur. Et quia hoc loco præponit Apostolus Principatus Potestatibus, Gregorius et Bernardus opinati sunt, Principatus ad secundam, Potestates vero ad infimam pertinere hierarchiam. Omnia per ipsum sicut per causam efficientem, et in ipso tanquam in exemplari principio, creata sunt, juxta intellectum jam dictum.
paras.en: [[1:16|For in him|Quia in ipso]], that is, through him, [[1:16|were all things created|condita sunt universa]]: for [[John 1:3|All things were made by him|omnia enim per ipsum facta sunt]], says the Evangelist. Or, [[1:16|in him|In ipso]], as in their exemplary principle, all things were created, that is, were disposed to be created. For the Son is the art full of reasons [that is, of the ideas of all things], and the exemplar of every creature. Therefore all things pre-exist in him as in their exemplar, and were foreordained and foreseen by the Father from eternity. For creatures are compared to him as things made by art to the artist, according to that saying of Wisdom: For of all things […] she is the worker, having all knowledge[[Wis 7:21||]] [no margin reference is printed; "the worker of all things" is Wis 7:21, and "having all knowledge" recalls Wis 7:23, "having all power"]. All things, then, were created in him, [[1:16|in heaven and on earth|in cœlis et in terra]], namely [[1:16|visible|visibilia]], such as the heavenly bodies and the elements, passive and mixed, [[1:16|and invisible|et invisibilia]], of which it is added: [[1:16|whether thrones|sive Throni]], that is, the angels of the lowest choir of the first and highest angelic hierarchy. They are called Thrones, that is, seats, because on account of their great nearness to God he is said to sit, rest and preside in them, and to exercise his judgements through them. [[1:16|or dominations, or principalities, or powers|Sive Dominationes, sive Principatus, sive Potestates]]. These three orders of angels the Apostle named to the Ephesians[[Eph 1:21||]], and enough seems to have been said of them there. And because in this place the Apostle puts the Principalities before the Powers, Gregory and Bernard held that the Principalities belong to the second hierarchy, the Powers to the lowest. [[1:16|All things were created by him|Omnia per ipsum]], as by their efficient cause, [[1:16|and in him|et in ipso]], as in their exemplary principle, in the sense already given.

paras.t: Et ipse Unigenitus Dei, est ante omnes, persistente æternitatis ævo atque incomparabili dignitate. Propter quod in Apocalypsi testatur: Ego sum Alpha et Omega, primus et novissimus, principium et finis. Et omnia in ipso constant, id est, idealiter et causaliter in eo exsistunt, juxta illud: Quod factum est, in ipso vita erat. Vel, In ipso constant, id est, ipsius divina potestate subsistunt, sustentantur, fulciuntur, junctaque permanent, prout Hebræis loquitur Apostolus: Portans omnia verbo virtutis suæ.
paras.en: [[1:17|And he|Et ipse]], the Only-begotten of God, [[1:17|is before all|est ante omnes]], by the abiding age of eternity and by incomparable dignity. Hence he testifies in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 22:13|I am Alpha and Omega, the First and the Last, the Beginning and the End|Ego sum Alpha et Omega, primus et novissimus, principium et finis]]. [[1:17|and by him all things consist|Et omnia in ipso constant]], that is, exist in him ideally and causally, according to that saying: [[John 1:3|that was made|Quod factum est]], [[John 1:4|In him was life|in ipso vita erat]]. Or, [[1:17|by him all things consist|In ipso constant]], that is, they subsist, are sustained and upheld, and hold together by his divine power, as the Apostle says to the Hebrews: [[Heb 1:3|upholding all things by the word of his power|Portans omnia verbo virtutis suæ]].

paras.t: Et ipse Christus est caput corporis Ecclesiæ, id est corporis mystici quod est Ecclesia. Quomodo autem intelligendum sit hoc, diffuse tractatum atque expositum est. Qui est principium omnium rerum, id est creator universorum. Unde quum ei dixissent Judæi, Tu quis es? respondit, Principium, qui et loquor vobis. Primogenitus ex mortuis, id est inter mortuos primus ad immortalem vitam resurgens. Nam qui ante eum suscitati fuerunt, rursus defuncti sunt. Ideo enim ait Scriptura: Qui est testis fidelis, primogenitus mortuorum. Vel, Primogenitus ex mortuis, id est inter mortuos suscitatos primus dignitate. Ut sit in omnibus angelis et hominibus; vel, In omnibus, id est præteritis, præsentibus ac futuris generationibus; ipse primatum tenens, id est universorum princeps et caput exsistens, sicut per Ecclesiasticum asserit: In omni gente et in omni populo primatum tenui. Habet enim in vestimento et in femore suo scriptum: Rex regum et Dominus dominantium. Et hoc, merito:
paras.en: [[1:18|And he|Et ipse]], Christ, [[1:18|is the head of the body, the church|est caput corporis Ecclesiæ]], that is, of the mystical body which is the Church. How this is to be understood has been treated and expounded at length[[Eph 1:22||]] [the margin gives "In Ephes. i, 22, 23": that is, in the commentary on that passage]. [[1:18|who is the beginning|Qui est principium]] of all things, that is, the creator of all. Hence when the Jews had said to him, [[John 8:25|Who art thou?|Tu quis es?]] he answered: [[John 8:25|The beginning, who also speak unto you|Principium, qui et loquor vobis]]. [[1:18|the firstborn from the dead|Primogenitus ex mortuis]], that is, the first among the dead to rise to immortal life; for those who were raised before him died again. For this reason Scripture says: [[Apoc 1:5|who is the faithful witness, the first begotten of the dead|Qui est testis fidelis, primogenitus mortuorum]]. Or, [[1:18|the firstborn from the dead|Primogenitus ex mortuis]], that is, first in dignity among the dead who are raised. [[1:18|that in all things|Ut sit in omnibus]], among angels and men; or, [[1:18|in all things|In omnibus]], that is, in generations past, present and to come, [[1:18|he may hold the primacy|ipse primatum tenens]], that is, being the prince and head of all, as he declares through Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 24:10|in every nation|In omni gente]] [[Ecclus 24:9|and in every people|et in omni populo]] [[Ecclus 24:10|I have had the chief rule|primatum tenui]]. For [[Apoc 19:16|he hath on his garment and on his thigh written: KING OF KINGS AND LORD OF LORDS|Habet enim in vestimento et in femore suo scriptum: Rex regum et Dominus dominantium]]. And this deservedly:

paras.t: Quia in ipso Christo prout est homo, complacuit Deo Trinitati omnem plenitudinem, id est plenam perfectionem scientiæ ac virtutum, inhabitare, id est stabiliter permanere. Non enim ad mensuram dat Deus Spiritum homini Christo. Et vidimus gloriam ejus, gloriam quasi Unigeniti a Patre, plenum gratiæ et veritatis. Vel, Omnem plenitudinem divinitatis, id est veram atque perfectam divinitatem, quemadmodum alio loco affirmat Apostolus: In ipso, inquiens, inhabitat omnis plenitudo divinitatis corporaliter.
paras.en: [[1:19|Because in him|Quia in ipso]], in Christ as he is man, [[1:19|it hath well pleased|complacuit]] God the Trinity [[1:19|that all fulness|omnem plenitudinem]], that is, the full perfection of knowledge and of the virtues, [[1:19|should dwell|inhabitare]], that is, abide stably. For [[John 3:34|God doth not give the Spirit by measure|Non enim ad mensuram dat Deus Spiritum]] to the man Christ. And [[John 1:14|we saw his glory, the glory as it were of the only begotten of the Father|Et vidimus gloriam ejus, gloriam quasi Unigeniti a Patre]], [[John 1:14|full of grace and truth|plenum gratiæ et veritatis]]. Or, [[1:19|all fulness|Omnem plenitudinem]] of the Godhead, that is, true and perfect Godhead, as the Apostle affirms in another place: [[Col 2:9|in him|In ipso]], he says, [[Col 2:9|dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead corporeally|inhabitat omnis plenitudo divinitatis corporaliter]].

paras.t: Placuit quoque Deo, et per eum, id est per Christi veneranda mysteria, reconciliare sibi ipsi omnia genera hominum in ipsum, id est ad hoc ut finaliter ad Deum convertantur, sicut ad beatitudinis fontem ac ultimum finem. Unde alibi dictum est: Deus erat in Christo, mundum reconcilians sibi; et in Isaia, Disciplina pacis nostræ super eum, et livore ejus sanati sumus. Pacificans Christus vel Trinitas per Christum, videlicet per sanguinem crucis ejus, id est pretiosissimo sanguine Christi in cruce effuso, sive quæ in cœlis sunt, sive quæ in terris, id est cœlestia et terrestria, utputa viatores et comprehensores de terra salvatos. Vel hoc ideo dicitur, quoniam angelos concordavit hominibus. Ipse siquidem est pax nostra, qui fecit utraque unum. Propter quod a Propheta vocatur Pater futuri sæculi, et princeps pacis. Et rursus per alium de Christo prædictum est: Loquetur pacem gentibus.
paras.en: It pleased God also, [[1:20|And through him|et per eum]], that is, through the venerable mysteries of Christ, [[1:20|to reconcile|reconciliare]] to himself [[1:20|all|omnia]] kinds of men [[1:20|unto himself|in ipsum]], that is, to this end, that they may at last be turned to God as to the fountain of beatitude and their last end. Hence it is said elsewhere: [[2 Cor 5:19|God indeed was in Christ, reconciling the world to himself|Deus erat in Christo, mundum reconcilians sibi]] [the margin gives I Cor. v, 19; the words are 2 Cor 5:19]; and in Isaias: [[Is 53:5|the chastisement of our peace was upon him, and by his bruises we are healed|Disciplina pacis nostræ super eum, et livore ejus sanati sumus]]. [[1:20|making peace|Pacificans]], Christ, or the Trinity through Christ, namely [[1:20|through the blood of his cross|per sanguinem crucis ejus]], that is, by the most precious blood of Christ shed on the cross, both [[1:20|the things that are in heaven|sive quæ in cœlis sunt]] and [[1:20|the things that are on earth|sive quæ in terris]], that is, heavenly and earthly things: for instance wayfarers and comprehensors [that is, those still on the way and the blessed who already possess God] saved from the earth. Or this is said because he has brought the angels into concord with men. For [[Eph 2:14|he is our peace, who hath made both one|Ipse siquidem est pax nostra, qui fecit utraque unum]]. For which reason he is called by the Prophet [[Is 9:6|the Father of the world to come, the Prince of Peace|Pater futuri sæculi, et princeps pacis]]. And again it was foretold of Christ through another: [[Zach 9:10|he shall speak peace to the Gentiles|Loquetur pacem gentibus]].

paras.t: Et vos, o Colossenses, quum essetis aliquando, scilicet tempore gentilitatis vestræ, alienati a Deo per idololatriam, et inimici sensu, id est intellectu, videlicet male sentiendo de Deo, per varios errores falsitatum fluctuando; vel, Sensu, id est sensualiter (id est juxta sensuum ductum) conversando; in operibus malis, id est vitiis carnis: nunc autem, tempore gratiæ, Christus reconciliavit vos Deo in corpore carnis ejus, id est per ea quæ pertulit in corpore suo, quod erat caro mortalis: ideo subditur, per mortem, id est per ejus beatissimam passionem, qua vivificatus est mundus; exhibere, id est ad hoc ut ipse exhibeat, quantum in se est, vel certe ut ipsi exhibeatis, vos sanctos in anima, et immaculatos a vitiis cunctis, et irreprehensibiles coram ipso, id est pure et reverenter vivendo in conspectu divino: quemadmodum ait Psalmista, Servavi mandata tua et testimonia tua, quia omnes viæ meæ in conspectu tuo. Tales autem eritis coram Deo, Christo vos præsentante Patri æterno, vel per propriorum operum ac meritorum vestrorum exhibitionem, quæ requiruntur ad obtinendam salutem. Qui enim creavit te sine te, id est sine tua cooperatione, non justificabit te sine te.
paras.en: [[1:21|And you|Et vos]], O Colossians, [[1:21|whereas you were some time|quum essetis aliquando]], namely in the time of your heathenism, [[1:21|alienated|alienati]] from God by idolatry, [[1:21|and enemies in mind|et inimici sensu]], that is, in understanding, namely by thinking ill of God and wavering through various errors and falsehoods; or, [[1:21|in mind|Sensu]], that is, living sensually (that is, by following the lead of the senses) [sensus: "mind" in the Douay-Rheims; the Latin word also means "sense", which gives Denis his second reading]; [[1:21|in evil works|in operibus malis]], that is, in the vices of the flesh: [[1:22|Yet now|nunc autem]], in the time of grace, Christ [[1:22|hath reconciled|reconciliavit]] you to God [[1:22|in the body of his flesh|in corpore carnis ejus]], that is, through what he suffered in his body, which was mortal flesh; therefore it is added, [[1:22|through death|per mortem]], that is, through his most blessed passion, by which the world was given life; [[1:22|to present|exhibere]], that is, to this end, that he may present, as far as in him lies, or else that you yourselves may present, [[1:22|you holy|vos sanctos]] in soul, [[1:22|and unspotted|et immaculatos]] from all vices, [[1:22|and blameless before him|et irreprehensibiles coram ipso]], that is, by living purely and reverently in the sight of God: as the Psalmist says, [[Ps 118:168|I have kept thy commandments and thy testimonies: because all my ways are in thy sight|Servavi mandata tua et testimonia tua, quia omnes viæ meæ in conspectu tuo]]. And you will be such before God through Christ presenting you to the eternal Father, or through the showing of your own works and merits, which are required for obtaining salvation. For he who created thee without thee, that is, without thy co-operation, will not justify thee without thee [a saying of Augustine, Sermon 169].

paras.t: Si tamen permanetis in fide fundati, firmiter integreque credendo, et stabiles in ea per opera bona, et immobiles a spe Evangelii quod audistis, id est ab exspectatione futuræ beatitudinis promissæ in Evangelio, quod prædicatum est in omnibus vestris per nos Apostolos aliosque discipulos, in universa creatura quæ sub cælo est, id est cunctis hominibus in terra degentibus, de quibus Christus aiebat: Prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ; cujus factus sum ego Deo auctore ego Paulus minister, id est prædicator.
paras.en: [[1:23|If so ye continue in the faith, grounded|Si tamen permanetis in fide fundati]], believing firmly and wholly, [[1:23|and settled|et stabiles]] in it through good works, [[1:23|and immoveable from the hope of the gospel which you have heard|et immobiles a spe Evangelii quod audistis]], that is, from the expectation of the future beatitude promised in the Gospel, [[1:23|which is preached|quod prædicatum est]] among all yours [so the text reads, in omnibus vestris; the sense is unclear] by us Apostles and other disciples, [[1:23|in all the creation that is under heaven|in universa creatura quæ sub cælo est]], that is, to all men living on earth, of whom Christ said: [[Mark 16:15|preach the gospel to every creature|Prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ]]; [[1:23|whereof|cujus]] [[1:23|I Paul|ego Paulus]] [[1:23|am made|factus sum]] [[1:23|a minister|minister]], by God's appointment, that is, a preacher.

paras.t: Qui etiam in Ephesso incarceratus, quæ dico in passionibus, id est in tribulatione: pro quibus patior, pro vobis, id est pro Ecclesia […]
paras.en: [[1:24|Who|Qui]] also, imprisoned at Ephesus, what I say [[1:24|in my sufferings|in passionibus]], that is, in tribulation: for which I suffer, [[1:24|for you|pro vobis]], that is, for the Church […] [the text of this passage is damaged, and its sense uncertain].

paras.t: Non est per hoc intelligendum, quod pœnæ quas Christus pro nobis sustinuit, incompletæ vel insufficientes fuerint ad mundi salvationem, ita ut Paulus, aut quisquam Sanctorum eas compleverit. Est igitur sensus: Et adimpleo, id est, longas et duras persecutiones ferendo, perficio ea quæ desunt, id est merita imperfecta, passionum Christi, id est propriarum afflictionum, quas in carne mea sustineo. Quæ propter unitatem Christi et membrorum ejus, dicuntur passiones Christi, juxta quod ipse dicebat: Saule, Saule, quid me persequeris? Juxta quem modum ait rursus per Prophetam Deus: Qui tetigerit vos, tanget pupillam oculi mei. Vel sic, quod redit tamen in idem: Adimpleo ea quæ desunt passionum Christi, id est passionum quas Christi amore, exemplo, jussione seu ordinatione sustineo. De quibus in Actibus dicebat Salvator: Ego ostendam illi quanta oporteat eum pro nomine meo pati. Hæc ergo sustineo sive adimpleo pro corpore ejus, id est pro mystico corpore Christi, quod est Ecclesia, videlicet ut fideles erudiam atque ædificem, eosque merito et numero augeam.
paras.en: This is not to be understood as though the pains which Christ bore for us were incomplete or insufficient for the salvation of the world, so that Paul or any of the saints should have completed them. The sense, then, is this: [[1:24|and fill up|Et adimpleo]], that is, by bearing long and hard persecutions I complete [[1:24|those things that are wanting|ea quæ desunt]], that is, the merits not yet complete, [[1:24|of the sufferings of Christ|passionum Christi]], that is, of my own afflictions, which I bear [[1:24|in my flesh|in carne mea]]. These, because of the unity of Christ and his members, are called the sufferings of Christ, according to what he himself said: [[Acts 9:4|Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?|Saule, Saule, quid me persequeris?]] In the same way God says again by the Prophet: [[Zach 2:8|he that toucheth you, toucheth the apple of my eye|Qui tetigerit vos, tanget pupillam oculi mei]]. Or thus, which yet comes to the same: [[1:24|fill up those things that are wanting of the sufferings of Christ|Adimpleo ea quæ desunt passionum Christi]], that is, of the sufferings which I bear for the love of Christ, after his example, at his command or by his ordinance; of which the Saviour said in the Acts: [[Acts 9:16|I will shew him how great things he must suffer for my name's sake|Ego ostendam illi quanta oporteat eum pro nomine meo pati]]. These, then, I bear or fill up [[1:24|for his body|pro corpore ejus]], that is, for the mystical body of Christ, [[1:24|which is the church|quod est Ecclesia]], namely so as to instruct and edify the faithful, and to increase them in merit and in number.

paras.t: Considerandum est enim, quod meritum passionis dominicæ et aliorum Sanctorum, imo et cetera opera supererogationis ipsorum, sunt velut res publica, ac thesaurus Ecclesiæ, de quo tam largæ indulgentiæ fiunt his qui per caritatem conjuncti et incorporati sunt Christo ac Sanctis. Hic autem thesaurus usque in finem mundi perficitur, ponentibus singulis quibusque Sanctorum partes suas in eo. Sicque Apostolus adimplevit ea quæ deerant passionum suarum, quotidie addidit quotidie aliquid huic thesauro.
paras.en: For it must be considered that the merit of the Lord's passion and of the other saints, and indeed their other works of supererogation [that is, good works beyond what is commanded], are as it were a common good [res publica: a common possession] and the treasury of the Church, from which such large indulgences are granted to those who are joined and incorporated by charity to Christ and the saints. And this treasury is being completed until the end of the world, each of the saints putting his own share into it. And so the Apostle filled up those things that were wanting of his sufferings, adding something to this treasury day after day.

paras.t: Cujus Christi vel Ecclesiæ factus sum ego minister, prædicando et sacramenta erogando, secundum dispensationem Dei, id est divinam ordinationem seu apostolatum mihi divinitus dispensatum; quæ dispensatio data est mihi in vobis, id est […]do ad effectum perducam, verbum Dei, id est divinam promissionem qua Deus Patriarchis Vatibusque promisit Evangelium Dei esse gentibus annuntiandum, et eas fore salvandas per fidem et gratiam Dei, quemadmodum per Isaiam loquitur: Mittam ex eis qui salvati fuerint, ad gentes in mare, in Africam et Lydiam, tenentes sagittam, in Italiam et Græciam, ad insulas longe; et annuntiabunt gloriam meam gentibus. Et quia dispositio, promissio, seu verbum illud, multum mirabile fuit atque occultum, ideo subditur:
paras.en: [[1:25|Whereof|Cujus]], that is, of Christ or of the Church, [[1:25|I am made a minister|factus sum ego minister]], by preaching and dispensing the sacraments, [[1:25|according to the dispensation of God|secundum dispensationem Dei]], that is, the divine ordinance, or the apostleship divinely dispensed to me; [[1:25|which|quæ]] dispensation [[1:25|is given me towards you|data est mihi in vobis]], that is, […] I may bring to effect, [[1:25|the word of God|verbum Dei]], that is, the divine promise by which God promised the patriarchs and prophets that the Gospel of God was to be announced to the Gentiles, and that they were to be saved by faith and the grace of God, as he speaks by Isaias: [[Is 66:19|I will send of them that shall be saved, to the Gentiles into the sea, into Africa, and Lydia them that draw the bow: into Italy, and Greece, to the islands afar off|Mittam ex eis qui salvati fuerint, ad gentes in mare, in Africam et Lydiam, tenentes sagittam, in Italiam et Græciam, ad insulas longe]]; [[Is 66:19|And they shall declare my glory to the Gentiles|et annuntiabunt gloriam meam gentibus]]. And because that disposition, promise or word was very wonderful and hidden, it is added:

paras.t: Mysterium, id est sacrum secretum, videlicet verbum præfatum, quod absconditum fuit, id est hominibus ignotum, a sæculis, id est a principio sæculorum, et a generationibus præcedentibus: non enim nisi paucis innotuit, et hoc, incomplete. De pleniori autem intellectu hujus scripturæ multa sunt ad Ephesios dicta, ubi quoque legitur: Mysterium Christi, quod aliis generationibus non est agnitum filiis hominum, sicut nunc revelatum est sanctis Apostolis, etc. Unde jam subditur: nunc autem, videlicet tempore gratiæ, manifestatum est mysterium istud per Christi prædicationem et Spiritus Sancti illustrationem, sanctis ejus, id est Apostolis et ceteris et primitivæ Ecclesiæ filiis, per quorum prædicationem manifestatum est ceteris populis, quibus voluit Deus notas facere divitias gloriæ, id est abundantem gloriam, sacramenti hujus, id est prædicti mysterii prædicati, in gentibus, id est inter gentes. In quo mysterio plurima spiritualia contenta sunt dona, quæ appellantur divitiæ gloriæ, utputa fides, indulgentia, reconciliatio, justitia, dona Spiritus Sancti, beatitudo futura.
paras.en: [[1:26|The mystery|Mysterium]], that is, the sacred secret, namely the word spoken of, [[1:26|which hath been hidden|quod absconditum fuit]], that is, unknown to men, [[1:26|from ages|a sæculis]], that is, from the beginning of the ages, [[1:26|and generations|et a generationibus]] that went before: for it was known only to a few, and that incompletely. Of the fuller understanding of this passage much was said on Ephesians, where we also read: [[Eph 3:4|the mystery of Christ|Mysterium Christi]], [[Eph 3:5|Which in other generations was not known to the sons of men, as it is now revealed to his holy apostles|quod aliis generationibus non est agnitum filiis hominum, sicut nunc revelatum est sanctis Apostolis]], etc. Hence it is now added: [[1:26|but now|nunc autem]], namely in the time of grace, [[1:26|is manifested|manifestatum est]] this mystery, by the preaching of Christ and the enlightening of the Holy Ghost, [[1:26|to his saints|sanctis ejus]], that is, to the Apostles and the other sons of the primitive Church, by whose preaching it has been made manifest to the other peoples, [[1:27|To whom God would make known the riches of the glory|quibus voluit Deus notas facere divitias gloriæ]], that is, abundant glory, [[1:27|of this mystery|sacramenti hujus]], that is, of the aforesaid mystery that was preached, [[1:27|among the Gentiles|in gentibus]], that is, amid the Gentiles. In this mystery very many spiritual gifts are contained, which are called the riches of glory: for instance faith, pardon, reconciliation, justice, the gifts of the Holy Ghost, the beatitude to come.

paras.t: Quod sacramentum est Christus materialiter, id est, Christus materia seu objectum est sacramenti istius, quia de ipso tractat et loquitur, qui est in vobis spes gloriæ, id est causa et ratio sperandi glorificationem beatam; quem nos annuntiamus, id est, gentibus prædicamus, corripientes omnem hominem præsentem et futurum, ad quem scripta nostra pervenerint, id est quosdam de omni genere hominum; vel, Omnem hominem, veritati fidei repugnantem; et docentes omnem hominem, id est quosdam de omnibus, in omni sapientia Scripturarum sanctarum ad salutem necessaria, ut exhibeamus omnem hominem perfectum in Christo Jesu, id est in fide, caritate et obsequio Christi, secundum exigentiam status præsentis: in quo nullus est perfectus simpliciter, vel ita ut ultra proficere aut perfici nequeat; sed sic, ut sine mortali vivat peccato, et passiones habeat reformatas, atque in virtutibus stabiliatur.
paras.en: Which mystery [[1:27|is Christ|est Christus]] materially, that is, Christ is the matter or object of this mystery, because it treats and speaks of him, who is [[1:27|in you the hope of glory|in vobis spes gloriæ]], that is, the cause and ground of hoping for blessed glorification; [[1:28|Whom we preach|quem nos annuntiamus]], that is, preach to the Gentiles, [[1:28|admonishing every man|corripientes omnem hominem]], present and to come, whom our writings shall reach, that is, some of every kind of men; or, [[1:28|every man|Omnem hominem]] who resists the truth of the faith [corripientes: "admonishing" in the Douay-Rheims; the word also means "rebuking"]; [[1:28|and teaching every man|et docentes omnem hominem]], that is, some of all, [[1:28|in all wisdom|in omni sapientia]] of the holy Scriptures that is necessary to salvation, [[1:28|that we may present every man perfect in Christ Jesus|ut exhibeamus omnem hominem perfectum in Christo Jesu]], that is, in the faith, charity and service of Christ, as the present state requires: in which no one is perfect simply, or so that he cannot advance or be perfected further, but in such a way that he lives without mortal sin, has his passions reformed, and is established in the virtues.

paras.t: In quo Christo, id est cujus amore; vel, in quo negotio consummando, videlicet ut exhibeam omnem hominem in Christo perfectum; et laboro die ac nocte, certando contra invisibiles ac visibiles hostes, secundum operationem, id est confortationem et influentiam, ejus, videlicet Christi, quam operatur in me, dando mihi auxilium gratiæ suæ ad efficaciter operandum; vel, Secundum operationem ejus in me, id est secundum operationem a me procedentem, quæ potius adscribenda est Christo quam mihi, juxta illud propheticum, Omnia opera nostra operatus es in nobis: quam operatur Christus in me in virtute, id est potenter seu propria sua divinaque potestate.
paras.en: [[1:29|Wherein|In quo]], that is, in Christ, for love of whom; or, in which task to be accomplished, namely that I may present every man perfect in Christ, [[1:29|also I labour|et laboro]] day and night, [[1:29|striving|certando]] against enemies invisible and visible, [[1:29|according to his working|secundum operationem]], that is, the strengthening and inflowing of him, namely of Christ, [[1:29|which he worketh in me|quam operatur in me]], giving me the help of his grace to work effectually; or, [[1:29|according to his working|Secundum operationem ejus]] in me, that is, according to the working that proceeds from me, which is to be ascribed to Christ rather than to me, according to that saying of the prophet: [[Is 26:12|thou hast wrought all our works for us|Omnia opera nostra operatus es in nobis]]; this working Christ works in me [[1:29|in power|in virtute]], that is, mightily, or by his own divine power.

2.title: ELUCIDATIO CAPITULI SECUNDI : VOLO ENIM VOS SCIRE QUALEM SOLLICITUDINEM HABEAM PRO VOBIS.
2.title_en: Elucidation of the second chapter: For I would have you know what manner of care I have for you.

paras.t: Cœptam in præcedenti capitulo exhortationem de vitandis cærimonialibus legis, prosequitur Apostolus in isto capitulo, admonens Colossenses ut falsos ac simulatos vitent doctores. Et ut sibi acquiescant facilius, manifestat quantum de eorum salute sollicitetur. Volo enim vos scire, ut amanti credatis, qualem sollicitudinem habeam pro vobis, et pro his qui sunt Laodiciæ (quæ est civitas Asiæ), id est pro vestra Laodicensiumque salute, ne ab impostoribus fallamini, a quibus præventi jam estis, et quicumque non viderunt faciem meam in carne, id est pro ceteris universis fidelibus quibus ipse in propria persona non prædicavi neque apparui. Ut consolentur corda ipsorum, id est, ob hoc sollicitus sum, quatenus corda ipsorum consolationem recipiant ex allocutione mea per epistolas, quæ consolata non sunt ex præsentia et immediata prædicatione mea; et sitis instructi, id est prudenter exercitati, in caritate, id est in actibus dilectionis Dei et proximi; vel, Instructi in caritate, id est de caritate Christi ad nos, ut sciatis et consideretis quantum Christus dilexerit nos, qui ait: Majorem hac dilectionem nemo habet, quam ut animam suam ponat quis pro amicis suis. Sitis quoque instructi, seu per caritatis instructionem tendentes, et in omnes divitias plenitudinis intellectus, id est perfectissimos habitus intellectuales, ut impleamini donis sapientiæ et intellectus, consilii atque scientiæ, in agnitionem mysterii, id est ad hoc ut actualiter consideretis mysterium, id est sacrum secretum, Dei Patris et Domini nostri Jesu Christi: per quod intelligi potest unitas Patris et Filii in essentia, et distinctio in persona; vel ipsa incarnatio, quæ est mysterium Patris tanquam auctoris, et Christi tanquam assumptoris vel exsecutoris.
paras.en: The exhortation begun in the preceding chapter about avoiding the ceremonies of the law the Apostle pursues in this chapter, warning the Colossians to shun false and feigned teachers. And so that they may the more readily heed him, he shows how anxious he is for their salvation. [[2:1|For I would have you know|Volo enim vos scire]], so that you may believe one who loves you, [[2:1|what manner of care I have for you and for them that are at Laodicea|qualem sollicitudinem habeam pro vobis, et pro his qui sunt Laodiciæ]] (which is a city of Asia), that is, for your salvation and that of the Laodiceans, lest you be deceived by impostors, by whom you have already been forestalled, [[2:1|and whosoever have not seen my face in the flesh|et quicumque non viderunt faciem meam in carne]], that is, for all the other faithful to whom I have not preached nor appeared in my own person. [[2:2|That their hearts may be comforted|Ut consolentur corda ipsorum]]: that is, I am anxious for this, that their hearts, which have not been comforted by my presence and my preaching in person, may receive comfort from my addressing them by letters; and that you may be [[2:2|instructed|instructi]], that is, prudently exercised, [[2:2|in charity|in caritate]], that is, in acts of love of God and of neighbour; or, Instructed in charity, that is, about the charity of Christ towards us, so that you may know and consider how much Christ has loved us, who says: [[John 15:13|Greater love than this no man hath, that a man lay down his life for his friends|Majorem hac dilectionem nemo habet, quam ut animam suam ponat quis pro amicis suis]]. May you also be instructed, or tending through the instruction of charity, [[2:2|and unto all riches of fulness of understanding|et in omnes divitias plenitudinis intellectus]], that is, unto the most perfect intellectual habits, so that you may be filled with the gifts of wisdom and understanding, of counsel and knowledge[[Is 11:2||]], [[2:2|unto the knowledge of the mystery|in agnitionem mysterii]], that is, to this end, that you may actually consider the mystery, that is, the sacred secret, [[2:2|of God the Father and of Christ Jesus|Dei Patris et Domini nostri Jesu Christi]]: by which may be understood the unity of the Father and the Son in essence and their distinction in person; or the incarnation itself, which is the mystery of the Father as its author, and of Christ as the one who assumed [our nature] and carried it out.

paras.t: In quo Christo sunt omnes thesauri, id est copiosissima plenitudo, sapientiæ divinorum et scientiæ creaturarum absconditi, id est incomprehensibiliter exsistentes. Christus namque secundum divinitatem, est ipsa æterna atque immensa sapientia, cujus non est numerus, estque increata scientia: cui convenit illud, O altitudo divitiarum sapientiæ et scientiæ Dei! Secundum humanitatem quoque assumptam, repletus est sapientia in contemplatione divinorum, et scientia in speculatione creaturarum, præsertim quum anima Christi præ universis Beatis, Divinitatem ac Trinitatem ab exordio suæ creationis clarius vidit, et omnia illa cognoscit quæ cognoscit et Verbum, scientia visionis, id est cuncta quæ unquam fuerunt, sunt aut erunt.
paras.en: [[2:3|In whom|In quo]], in Christ, [[2:3|are hid all the treasures|sunt omnes thesauri]], that is, the most abundant fulness, [[2:3|of wisdom|sapientiæ]] of divine things [[2:3|and knowledge|et scientiæ]] of creatures, [[2:3|hid|absconditi]], that is, existing incomprehensibly. For Christ according to His divinity is that eternal and immense wisdom of which there is no number[[Ps 146:5||]], and is uncreated knowledge, to whom applies that word: [[Rom 11:33|O the depth of the riches of the wisdom and of the knowledge of God!|O altitudo divitiarum sapientiæ et scientiæ Dei!]] According to the humanity He assumed, too, He is filled with wisdom in contemplating divine things and with knowledge in considering creatures, above all since the soul of Christ, beyond all the Blessed, saw the Godhead and the Trinity more clearly from the first moment of its creation, and knows all that the Word knows by the knowledge of vision [that is, knowledge of what actually exists at any time, as distinct from the merely possible], that is, all things that ever were, are, or will be.

paras.t: Hoc autem dico, ut nemo vos decipiat, id est, fidei vestræ simplicitatem inficiat, in sublimitate sermonis, id est per verba profunda secundum apparentiam, et fucata seu subtilia argumenta. Denique ista admoneo: Nam etsi corpore absum a vobis, id est a vobis distans loco ac corporali separatione, sed spiritu, id est mentis consideratione, vobiscum sum, tum quia de vobis sæpius cogito, tum quia in spiritu prophetico quasi præsens inspicio quid agatis: quemadmodum Eliseus præsens fuit quando Giezi accepit munera Naaman; gaudens in Domino de vestro profectu, et videns, id est cognoscens, ordinem vestrum, id est vitæ vestræ ordinationem, quomodo omnia honeste et secundum ordinem fiunt in vobis, et firmamentum ejus quæ in Christo est fidei vestræ, id est stabilitatem seu robur fidei vestræ quam in Christo habetis.
paras.en: [[2:4|Now this I say, that no man may deceive you|Hoc autem dico, ut nemo vos decipiat]], that is, corrupt the simplicity of your faith, [[2:4|by loftiness of words|in sublimitate sermonis]], that is, by words profound in appearance and by specious or subtle arguments. Moreover I give this warning: [[2:5|For though I be absent in body|Nam etsi corpore absum]] from you, that is, distant from you in place and bodily separation, [[2:5|yet in spirit|sed spiritu]], that is, in the regard of my mind, [[2:5|I am with you|vobiscum sum]], both because I often think of you, and because in the prophetic spirit I see, as if present, what you are doing: just as Eliseus was present when Giezi took the gifts of Naaman[[4 Kings 5:1||]]; [[2:5|rejoicing|gaudens]] in the Lord at your progress, [[2:5|and beholding|et videns]], that is, knowing, [[2:5|your order|ordinem vestrum]], that is, the ordering of your life, how all things are done among you decently and according to order[[1 Cor 14:40||]], [[2:5|and the steadfastness of your faith which is in Christ|et firmamentum ejus quæ in Christo est fidei vestræ]], that is, the stability or strength of the faith that you have in Christ.

paras.t: Consequenter hortatur eos ad perseverantiam ac profectum in bonis. Sicut ergo accepistis Christum Jesum Dominum nostrum, id est, sicut credendo cœpistis conversari in Christo, in ipso ambulate, id est, sic exinde in eo procedite, proficiendo semper in melius, per imitationem vestigiorum Salvatoris. Sola namque perseverantia coronatur. Radicati, id est firmiter fixi, per modum radicis terræ inhærentis, et superædificati in ipso, id est in doctrina et gratia Christi, ita ut sitis domus seu habitaculum Dei, cujus fundamentum sit Christus seu doctrina et gratia ejus. Unde Ephesiis dictum est: Superædificati super fundamentum Apostolorum et Prophetarum. Et confirmati in fide, ut nec philosophicis rationibus, nec sensuum apparentiis, nec persecutionibus, recedatis a fidei sinceritate, sicut et didicistis ab Archippo ambulandum esse et standum in fide, qua nutante, tota virtutum structura vacillat, abundantes in illo in gratiarum actione, id est Deo copiose grates referendo.
paras.en: Next he exhorts them to perseverance and progress in good. [[2:6|As therefore you have received Jesus Christ the Lord|Sicut ergo accepistis Christum Jesum Dominum nostrum]], that is, as by believing you began to live in Christ, [[2:6|walk ye in him|in ipso ambulate]], that is, so henceforth go forward in Him, ever advancing to better, by following in the footsteps of the Saviour. For perseverance alone is crowned[[Matt 10:22||]]. [[2:7|Rooted|Radicati]], that is, firmly fixed, like a root clinging to the earth, [[2:7|and built up in him|et superædificati in ipso]], that is, in the doctrine and grace of Christ, so that you may be a house or dwelling of God whose foundation is Christ, or His doctrine and grace. Hence it was said to the Ephesians: [[Eph 2:20|Built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets|Superædificati super fundamentum Apostolorum et Prophetarum]]. [[2:7|And confirmed in the faith|Et confirmati in fide]], so that neither by philosophical reasonings, nor by the appearances of the senses, nor by persecutions, you depart from the purity of the faith, [[2:7|as also you have learned|sicut et didicistis]] from Archippus, that one must walk and stand in the faith, for if it totters the whole structure of the virtues shakes; [[2:7|abounding in him in thanksgiving|abundantes in illo in gratiarum actione]], that is, giving thanks to God abundantly.

paras.t: Advertendum autem, quod triplici via conabantur perversi hos Colossenses subvertere, scilicet, per philosophiam, per legis allegationem, per simulatam sanctitatem. Hos processus Apostolus reprobat. Videte ne quis vos decipiat per philosophiam, id est scientiam naturalem, studio philosophorum inventam, et inanem fallaciam, id est per argumenta sophistica, quæ videntur aliquid probare, sed non probant veraciter: philosophiam, inquam, procedentem ac judicantem secundum traditionem hominum, id est humanæ rationis discursum, secundum elementa hujus mundi, id est juxta ea quæ naturaliter apparent in rebus, videlicet secundum causas naturales et elementares, et solitum cursum rerum, et non secundum Christum: id est, deceptores isti atque philosophi, non secundum Christi doctrinam procedunt, considerando divinæ virtutis illimitatam potentiam, non determinatam ad naturalem ac solitum cursum seu ordinem rerum, sed supernaturalia et nobis incomprehensibilia operari valentem. In quo declaratur philosophorum fatuitas, asserentium Deum non posse aliquid agere præter naturalem ordinem rerum, et ultra humanæ rationis capacitatem. Propter quod negabant quidquid rationem excedit, videlicet Deum incarnatum, virginem peperisse, etc. — Cur autem his qui non procedunt secundum Christum, debeat contradici, subjungitur: quia in ipso, id est in Christi humana natura quasi in templo, habitat omnis plenitudo divinitatis, id est perfecta veraque divinitas cum omni sua perfectione. Personaliter enim in Christo unitæ sunt natura divina et humana. Habitat autem in ea corporaliter, id est, corpori ejus vere ac immediate conjuncta est, sicut et animæ ejus, non quod ipsa sit corpus. Porro divinitas dicitur sic unita, quoniam persona Verbi, quæ est divinitas, humanitati conjuncta est.
paras.en: Now note that the perverse were trying to subvert these Colossians in three ways: by philosophy, by appeal to the law, and by feigned holiness. These approaches the Apostle condemns. [[2:8|Beware lest any man cheat you by philosophy|Videte ne quis vos decipiat per philosophiam]], that is, natural science, discovered by the study of the philosophers, [[2:8|and vain deceit|et inanem fallaciam]], that is, by sophistical arguments, which seem to prove something but do not truly prove it: philosophy, I say, proceeding and judging [[2:8|according to the tradition of men|secundum traditionem hominum]], that is, the reasoning of human understanding, [[2:8|according to the elements of the world|secundum elementa hujus mundi]], that is, according to what appears naturally in things, namely according to natural and elementary causes and the usual course of things, [[2:8|and not according to Christ|et non secundum Christum]]: that is, these deceivers and philosophers do not proceed according to the doctrine of Christ, by considering the unlimited might of the divine power, which is not bound to the natural and usual course or order of things, but is able to work things supernatural and incomprehensible to us. In this is shown the folly of the philosophers who assert that God cannot do anything beyond the natural order of things and beyond the capacity of human reason. For this reason they denied whatever exceeds reason, namely that God became incarnate, that a virgin gave birth, and so on. — Why those who do not proceed according to Christ ought to be opposed is added: [[2:9|For in him|quia in ipso]], that is, in Christ's human nature as in a temple, [[2:9|dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead|habitat omnis plenitudo divinitatis]], that is, perfect and true divinity with all its perfection. For in Christ the divine and human natures are united in one person. And it dwells in that nature [[2:9|corporeally|corporaliter]], that is, it is truly and immediately joined to His body, as also to His soul, not that it is itself a body. Moreover the divinity is said to be so united because the person of the Word, which is the divinity, is joined to the humanity.

paras.t: Deinceps ostendit Apostolus vanam esse rationem eorum qui per legis allegationem nitebantur Colossenses subvertere, inducendo eos ad cærimonialia legis. Et estis in illo, id est a Christo prout Deus est, et per ipsum prout est homo, Dei ac hominum mediator, repleti gratia et donis Spiritus Sancti, ita ut nequaquam indigeatis legalium observantia. Propterea scriptum est: De plenitudine ejus nos accepimus omnes gratiam pro gratia. Ipse quoque propter nos egenus factus est, ut ejus inopia divites essemus. Qui Christus, etiam secundum naturam assumptam, est caput, id est capitalis influxor, omnis principatus et potestatis, id est angelorum sanctorum: qui omnes a Christo homine purgantur, illuminantur ac perficiuntur, secundum Theologum.
paras.en: Next the Apostle shows the reasoning of those to be empty who were trying to subvert the Colossians by appeal to the law, leading them to the ceremonies of the law. [[2:10|And you are filled in him|Et estis in illo]], that is, by Christ as He is God, and through Him as He is man, the mediator of God and men[[1 Tim 2:5||]], [[2:10|filled|repleti]] with the grace and gifts of the Holy Ghost, so that you have no need at all of the observance of the legal ceremonies. Therefore it is written: [[John 1:16|And of his fulness we all have received: and grace for grace|De plenitudine ejus nos accepimus omnes gratiam pro gratia]]. He also became poor for our sakes, that through His poverty we might be rich[[2 Cor 8:9||]]. [[2:10|Who|Qui]], Christ, even according to the nature He assumed, [[2:10|is the head|est caput]], that is, the one who flows into them as head, [[2:10|of all principality and power|omnis principatus et potestatis]], that is, of the holy angels, who are all purified, enlightened and perfected by Christ as man, according to the Theologian [that is, Dionysius the Areopagite].

paras.t: In quo, id est cujus virtute, operatione et gratia, circumcisi estis circumcisione non manufacta, id est non carnali, legali ac litterali, in exspoliatione corporis carnis, id est amittendo particulam corporis quod est caro, videlicet pellem præputii quæ in illa circumcisione aufertur, sed in circumcisione Jesu Christi, id est, spirituali atque a Christo facta circumcisione circumcisi estis per expurgationem superfluitatis vitiorum ac passionum vestrarum. De qua circumcisione scriptum est: Circumcidimini Domino, et auferte præputia cordium vestrorum; et iterum alibi, Circumcidite præputium cordis vestri, et cervicem vestram ne induretis amplius.
paras.en: [[2:11|In whom|In quo]], that is, by whose power, working and grace, [[2:11|you are circumcised with circumcision not made by hand|circumcisi estis circumcisione non manufacta]], that is, not carnal, legal and literal, [[2:11|in despoiling of the body of the flesh|in exspoliatione corporis carnis]], that is, by losing a small part of the body that is flesh, namely the skin of the foreskin, which is removed in that circumcision; [[2:11|but in the circumcision of Christ|sed in circumcisione Jesu Christi]], that is, you are circumcised with a spiritual circumcision made by Christ, by the purging away of the excess of your vices and passions. Of this circumcision it is written: [[Jer 4:4|Be circumcised to the Lord, and take away the foreskins of your hearts|Circumcidimini Domino, et auferte præputia cordium vestrorum]]; and again elsewhere: [[Deut 10:16|Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and stiffen your neck no more|Circumcidite præputium cordis vestri, et cervicem vestram ne induretis amplius]].

paras.t: Consepulti ei, videlicet Christo, in Baptismo, id est in susceptione Baptismatis omnino vitiis mortificati, sicut et Christi corpus in sepulcro mortuum erat naturali vitæ. Vel hoc ideo dicitur, quoniam baptizati ter tinguntur in aqua, quemadmodum Christus triduo erat in monumento; et sicut Christus de sepulcro ad immortalem vitam surrexit, sic baptizati de sepulcro a vitiorum corruptione ac vetustate liberati ascendunt. Ideo subditur: in quo Christo et resurrexistis a ruina peccati, per fidem operationis Dei, id est per fidem quam Deus operatur seu creat in vobis: sine fide enim nemo spiritualiter surgit; qui Deus Pater vel Trinitas suscitavit illum a mortuis tertia die.
paras.en: [[2:12|Buried with him|Consepulti ei]], that is, with Christ, [[2:12|in baptism|in Baptismo]], that is, wholly dead to vices in receiving Baptism, as the body of Christ in the tomb was dead to natural life. Or this is said because the baptized are dipped three times in the water, as Christ was three days in the tomb; and as Christ rose from the tomb to immortal life, so the baptized come up from the tomb freed from the corruption and oldness of vices. Hence it is added: [[2:12|in whom also you are risen again|in quo et resurrexistis]], in Christ, from the fall of sin, [[2:12|by the faith of the operation of God|per fidem operationis Dei]], that is, by the faith which God works or creates in you: for without faith no one rises spiritually; [[2:12|who hath raised him up from the dead|qui suscitavit illum a mortuis]], that is, God the Father, or the Trinity, on the third day.

paras.t: Et vos quum mortui essetis spiritualiter, carentes vita gratiæ, in delictis, id est propter peccata vestra quibus naturalem legem reliquistis, et præputio carnis vestræ, id est propter carnalia vitia, vel propter originale peccatum quod per præputium traducitur, convivificavit cum illo, id est, ad vitam gratiæ suscitavit, quemadmodum Christum ad vitam naturalem humanam reduxit, suscitando eum a mortuis: vel, Convivificavit cum illo, id est, immortalitatem vobis jam dedit in spe, quam Christo dedit in re. Capitis namque præcessio, spes est membrorum. Donans, id est, gratis et sine merito vestro dimittens, vobis omnia delicta vestra merito Christi, dummodo tamen meritum illud vobis applicetur per fidem vel sacramenta Ecclesiæ.
paras.en: [[2:13|And you, when you were dead|Et vos quum mortui essetis]] spiritually, lacking the life of grace, [[2:13|in your sins|in delictis]], that is, through your sins by which you forsook the natural law, [[2:13|and the uncircumcision of your flesh|et præputio carnis vestræ]], that is, through carnal vices, or through original sin, which is handed down through the foreskin [that is, through carnal generation], [[2:13|he hath quickened together with him|convivificavit cum illo]], that is, raised you to the life of grace, as He brought Christ back to natural human life by raising Him from the dead; or, He hath quickened together with him, that is, He has already given you in hope the immortality He gave Christ in reality. For the going-before of the Head is the hope of the members. [[2:13|Forgiving|Donans]], that is, remitting freely and without your merit, [[2:13|you all offences|vobis omnia delicta]] of yours, by the merit of Christ, provided however that this merit be applied to you through faith or the sacraments of the Church.

paras.t: Delens ipse Christus, merito passionis suæ, quod adversum nos erat chirographum decreti, id est memoriale seu litteram humanæ transgressionis, qua homo protoplastus prævaricatus est in paradiso decretum, id est Dei præceptum. Hujus enim transgressionis memor fuit Deus ad puniendum, dæmon ad accusandum. Habuitque diabolus quasi litteram testimonialem reatus quem homo incurrit transgrediendo divinum præceptum, imo et tota posteritas primi parentis. Christus vero satisfaciendo pro peccatis nostris actualibus ac originalibus, eripuit totum genus humanum ab isto reatu, seu debito pœnæ pro peccato infligendæ. Et ita delevit prædictum chirographum, quod contra nos erat, quoniam erat testimonium faciens nos damnationi obnoxios. Quum vero peccatum dimittitur, dicimus Deum oblivisci illius. Dæmon quoque non potest de illo peccato accusationem efficacem obtendere. Quod chirographum erat contrarium nobis: sicut jam dictum est. Et ipsum tulit de medio, id est, ab universis hominibus abstulit illud chirographum, affigens illud cruci, id est, in sua passione illud occidens seu destruens, quantum in se erat. Eripuit enim nos de pœna pro peccato originali post hanc vitam infligenda, dummodo ei ut capiti uniamur per fidem et caritatem, quatenus virtus suæ passionis redundet in nos tanquam in membra ipsius.
paras.en: [[2:14|Blotting out|Delens]], Christ Himself, by the merit of His passion, [[2:14|the handwriting of the decree that was against us|quod adversum nos erat chirographum decreti]], that is, the record or written bond of human transgression, by which the first-formed man in paradise transgressed the decree[[Gen 3:6||]], that is, the commandment of God. For God kept this transgression in mind to punish it, the devil to accuse it. And the devil held, as it were, a written testimony of the guilt which man incurred by transgressing the divine commandment, and indeed the whole posterity of the first parent with him. But Christ, by making satisfaction for our actual and original sins, rescued the whole human race from this guilt, or debt of punishment to be inflicted for sin. And so He blotted out the said handwriting that was against us, since it was a testimony making us liable to damnation. Now when sin is forgiven, we say that God forgets it. Nor can the devil bring any effective accusation about that sin. [[2:14|Which was contrary to us|Quod erat contrarium nobis]], the handwriting, as has just been said. [[2:14|And he hath taken the same out of the way|Et ipsum tulit de medio]], that is, He took away that handwriting from all men, [[2:14|fastening it to the cross|affigens illud cruci]], that is, in His passion slaying or destroying it, as far as lay in Him. For He rescued us from the punishment to be inflicted after this life for original sin, provided we be united to Him as our head by faith and charity, so that the power of His passion may overflow into us as into His members.

paras.t: Et exspolians principatus et potestates, id est, dæmones superiores ac inferiores privans præda quam ceperant, puta animabus seu hominibus quos suo dominio subdiderant inducendo eos ad culpam. De hac exspoliatione ait ipse Salvator: Nunc princeps hujus mundi ejicietur foras: et item, Ego, inquit, si exaltatus fuero a terra, omnia traham ad me ipsum. Christus namque est qui domum adversarii nostri ingressus est, fortemque armatum alligavit, ac vasa ejus diripuit. Propter quod jubetur per Prophetam Christus vocari, Accelera, spolia detrahe, festina prædari. Traduxit confidenter, id est, prædam hanc dæmoni ablatam Christus securissime transtulit in regnum suum, præsidens eis quibus præsidebat diabolus. Nunc enim ponit eos in regno Ecclesiæ militantis, postea autem ponet eos (sicut jam plurimos posuit) in regno Ecclesiæ triumphantis. Palam triumphans, id est evidenter vincens, illos, id est diabolos, in semetipso, id est in proprii corporis crucifixione; vel, In semetipso, id est in propria persona ad inferos descendendo, et sanctos educendo, implens illud propheticum: De manu mortis liberabo eos, de morte redimam eos; ero mors tua, o mors, morsus tuus ero, inferne.
paras.en: [[2:15|And despoiling the principalities and powers|Et exspolians principatus et potestates]], that is, depriving the higher and lower demons of the prey they had taken, namely souls or men, whom they had brought under their dominion by leading them into sin. Of this despoiling the Saviour Himself says: [[John 12:31|now shall the prince of this world be cast out|Nunc princeps hujus mundi ejicietur foras]]; and again: [[John 12:32|And I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all things to myself|Ego, inquit, si exaltatus fuero a terra, omnia traham ad me ipsum]]. For it is Christ who entered the house of our adversary, bound the strong man armed, and plundered his goods[[Matt 12:29||]].
