For this reason Christ is ordered by the Prophet to be called: Hasten to take away the spoils, make haste to take the prey[[Is 8:3||]] [the name *Maher-shalal-hash-baz* given in Isaias 8:3, which the Vulgate translates]. [[2:15|He hath exposed them confidently|Traduxit confidenter]], that is, Christ most securely carried this prey, taken from the devil, over into His kingdom, ruling over those whom the devil ruled. For now He places them in the kingdom of the Church militant, and later He will place them (as He has already placed very many) in the kingdom of the Church triumphant. [[2:15|In open shew, triumphing|Palam triumphans]], that is, manifestly conquering, [[2:15|over them|illos]], that is, the devils, [[2:15|in himself|in semetipso]], that is, in the crucifixion of His own body; or, In himself, that is, in His own person, by descending to hell and leading out the saints, fulfilling that prophecy: [[Osee 13:14|I will deliver them out of the hand of death. I will redeem them from death: O death, I will be thy death; O hell, I will be thy bite|De manu mortis liberabo eos, de morte redimam eos; ero mors tua, o mors, morsus tuus ero, inferne]].

paras.t: Ex his concludit Apostolus principale intentum, videlicet, quod non teneantur fideles ad observationem legalium post Christi passionem. Nemo ergo, id est, quum prædicta se ita habeant, nemo vos judicet, id est, damnabiles asserat, in cibo aut in potu, id est in usu victus, scilicet ob id quod non discernatis inter cibos more Judaico, aut in parte diei festi, id est ex parte omissionis Judaicarum celebritatum, videlicet aut neomeniæ, id est festi occurrentis in novilunio, aut sabbatorum, id est ultimorum dierum hebdomadæ; quæ omnia sunt umbra futurorum, id est obscura signa eorum quæ in novo Testamento geruntur: prout alibi dicit Apostolus, Umbram habens lex futurorum bonorum, non ipsam imaginem rerum; corpus autem Christi, id est, veritas per illa significata, per Christum impletur, ad eumque pertinet. Ideo Christi mysteriis consummatis, quando in cruce dicebat, Consummatum est, quando et velum templi scissum est, legalia cessaverunt, sicut figura cessat adveniente re figurata.
paras.en: From this the Apostle draws his principal point, namely that the faithful are not bound to observe the legal ceremonies after the passion of Christ. [[2:16|Let no man therefore|Nemo ergo]], that is, since the foregoing is so, let no man [[2:16|judge you|vos judicet]], that is, declare you worthy of condemnation, [[2:16|in meat or in drink|in cibo aut in potu]], that is, in the use of food, namely because you do not distinguish between foods in the Jewish manner, [[2:16|or in respect of a festival day|aut in parte diei festi]], that is, on account of omitting the Jewish solemnities, namely [[2:16|or of the new moon|aut neomeniæ]], that is, the feast falling at the new moon, [[2:16|or of the sabbaths|aut sabbatorum]], that is, of the last days of the week; [[2:17|which|quæ]] all [[2:17|are a shadow of things to come|sunt umbra futurorum]], that is, obscure signs of what is accomplished in the New Testament: as the Apostle says elsewhere: [[Heb 10:1|For the law, having a shadow of the good things to come, not the very image of the things|Umbram habens lex futurorum bonorum, non ipsam imaginem rerum]]; [[2:17|but the body is of Christ|corpus autem Christi]], that is, the truth signified by them is fulfilled through Christ and belongs to Him. Therefore, when the mysteries of Christ were accomplished, when He said on the cross, [[John 19:30|It is consummated|Consummatum est]], when also the veil of the temple was rent[[Matt 27:51||]], the legal ceremonies ceased, as the figure ceases when the thing figured arrives.

paras.t: Præterea agit Apostolus contra eos qui per simulatam sanctitatem nitebantur subvertere Colossenses. Nemo vos seducat, volens, id est suadere contendens, in humilitate et religione angelorum, id est per fictam humilitatem et apparentem religionem, quibus angelis similis videtur, tanquam verus nuntius Dei, sicut et angelus, quæ non vidit, id est observationes legalium quæ non intellexit secundum spiritualem et mysticam rationem, videlicet prout sunt signa futuri: hoc est, cupiens probare hac circumventione legalia esse servanda: qui est ambulans frustra, id est infructuose laborans, inflatus sensu carnis suæ, id est tumidus et superbus intellectu carnali, carnaliter intelligente legalia, et sensualitatem ac imaginationem potius quam spiritualem rationem sequente, sapiens in oculis propriis; et non tenens caput, id est Christo non inhærens, ex quo totum corpus, id est universa Ecclesia, per nexus fidei et conjunctiones sanctæ dilectionis subministratum, id est exhibitum, vel sibi invicem subserviens, et constructum, id est in unum redactum, hoc est spiritualiter copulatum per fidem, spem, caritatem, et opera atque obsequia pia, quibus uniuntur et unum mysticum corpus efficiuntur fideles: quod corpus hoc modo compactum, crescit in augmentum Dei, id est in magnitudinem spiritualem, videlicet in incrementum virtutum per gratiam et efficientiam Dei.
paras.en: Further, the Apostle deals with those who were trying to subvert the Colossians by feigned holiness. [[2:18|Let no man seduce you, willing|Nemo vos seducat, volens]], that is, striving to persuade, [[2:18|in humility and religion of angels|in humilitate et religione angelorum]], that is, by feigned humility and apparent religion, by which he seems like the angels, as if he were a true messenger of God, as an angel is; [[2:18|the things which he hath not seen|quæ non vidit]], that is, the legal observances, which he has not understood according to their spiritual and mystical meaning, namely as signs of what was to come: that is, wishing by this trickery to prove that the legal ceremonies must be kept; who is [[2:18|walking in the things which he hath not seen, in vain|ambulans frustra]], that is, labouring fruitlessly, [[2:18|puffed up by the sense of his flesh|inflatus sensu carnis suæ]], that is, swollen and proud with a carnal understanding, which understands the legal ceremonies carnally and follows sensuality and imagination rather than spiritual reason, wise in his own eyes[[Is 5:21||]]; [[2:19|And not holding the head|et non tenens caput]], that is, not clinging to Christ, [[2:19|from which the whole body|ex quo totum corpus]], that is, the whole Church, [[2:19|by joints|per nexus]] of faith [[2:19|and bands|et conjunctiones]] of holy love, [[2:19|being supplied with nourishment|subministratum]], that is, furnished, or serving one another, [[2:19|and compacted|et constructum]], that is, brought into one, that is, spiritually joined by faith, hope, charity, and good works and services, by which the faithful are united and made one mystical body[[Rom 12:5||]]: which body, thus compacted, [[2:19|groweth into the increase of God|crescit in augmentum Dei]], that is, into spiritual greatness, namely into the increase of the virtues by the grace and working of God.

paras.t: Si ergo mortui estis cum Christo, id est a vitiis mortificati ac purificati, sicut et Christus semper a vitiis immunissimus fuit: mortui, inquam, ab elementis hujus mundi, id est ab inordinato affectu et cultu sensibilium ac sæcularium rerum; vel, Mortui cum Christo, id est, si Christo adhærentes, separati estis ab elementis hujus mundi, id est a lege, ejusque cærimonialibus præceptis, in quibus est institutio puerorum, mundana quærentium. In lege namque quasi in elementis alphabeti, est litteralis ac puerilis institutio. Quid adhuc, id est usque in præsens, videlicet evangelica veritate jam patefacta, tanquam viventes in mundo, id est quasi sæcularem vitam ducentes, non Deo viventes, decernitis, id est, determinatis legalia esse servanda? dicentes ad invicem: Ne tetigeritis, neque gustaveritis, neque contrectaveritis ea quæ lex prohibet tangi, gustari aut contrectari.
paras.en: [[2:20|If then you be dead with Christ|Si ergo mortui estis cum Christo]], that is, mortified and purified from vices, as Christ was ever wholly free from vices: dead, I say, [[2:20|from the elements of this world|ab elementis hujus mundi]], that is, from inordinate affection for and devotion to sensible and worldly things; or, Dead with Christ, that is, if, cleaving to Christ, you are separated from the elements of this world, that is, from the law and its ceremonial precepts, in which lies the schooling of children who seek worldly things. For in the law, as in the elements [that is, the letters] of the alphabet, there is a literal and childish schooling. [[2:20|Why do you yet|quid adhuc]], that is, up to the present, namely now that the gospel truth has been revealed, [[2:20|as though living in the world|tanquam viventes in mundo]], that is, as leading a worldly life, not living to God, [[2:20|decree|decernitis]], that is, determine that the legal ceremonies must be kept? saying to one another: [[2:21|Touch not: taste not: handle not.|Ne tetigeritis, neque gustaveritis, neque contrectaveritis:]] the things which the law forbids to be touched, tasted or handled.

paras.t: Quæ sunt omnia in interitum, id est, ista decernere, seu legalia observare, mortem spiritualem inducunt, ipso usu, id est per hoc quod Judaico ritu servantur, secundum præcepta et doctrinas hominum, id est, prout a Pharisæis et Scribis jubentur et persuadentur servari post Christi passionem. Quamvis enim præcepta cærimonialia fuerint divinitus data, et suo tempore observanda, tamen ut observentur tempore novæ legis non est secundum præceptum doctrinamque Dei, sed hominum Judæorum.
paras.en: [[2:22|Which all are unto destruction|Quæ sunt omnia in interitum]], that is, to decree these things, or to observe the legal ceremonies, brings on spiritual death, [[2:22|by the very use|ipso usu]], that is, by their being kept in the Jewish rite, [[2:22|according to the precepts and doctrines of men|secundum præcepta et doctrinas hominum]], that is, as they are commanded and urged to be kept after Christ's passion by the Pharisees and Scribes. For although the ceremonial precepts were given by God and were to be observed in their own time, yet that they should be observed in the time of the new law is not according to the precept and doctrine of God, but of men, the Jews.

paras.t: Quæ præcepta, tempore gratiæ, sunt rationem quidem habentia sapientiæ, id est, speciem sapientiæ habent, non essentiam: habentque apparentiam seu speciem hanc in superstitione, quia videntur ad superexcedentem religionem pertinere, et humilitate simulata, quoniam observatores eorum humilitatem confingunt, et Deo obedire se simulant; et quia sunt non ad parcendum corpori, quoniam observatio legalium laboriosissima est, sicque videtur pertinere ad rigorem justitiæ, non ad carnalitatem; ideo etiam, quia sunt non in honore aliquo, id est, humanum honorem non quærunt observatores eorum, permittentes carnem præputii sui circumcidi; et quia non sunt ad saturitatem carnis, id est, etiam ideo speciem sapientiæ habent legalia hæc, quoniam multa delectabilia subtrahunt corpori, ut carnes porcinas: unde videntur ad sobrietatem et abstinentiam pertinere: propter quod observatores eorum, judicant non observantes esse gulosos.
paras.en: [[2:23|Which things|Quæ]] precepts, in the time of grace, [[2:23|have indeed a shew of wisdom|sunt rationem quidem habentia sapientiæ]], that is, they have the appearance of wisdom, not its substance: and they have this appearance or show [[2:23|in superstition|in superstitione]], because they seem to belong to an exceeding religion, [[2:23|and humility|et humilitate]] feigned, since those who observe them make a show of humility and pretend to obey God; [[2:23|and|et]] because they are [[2:23|not sparing the body|non ad parcendum corpori]], since the observance of the legal ceremonies is most laborious, and so seems to belong to the rigour of justice, not to carnality; and also because they are [[2:23|not in any honour|non in honore aliquo]], that is, those who observe them do not seek human honour, allowing the flesh of their foreskin to be circumcised; and because they are not [[2:23|to the filling of the flesh|ad saturitatem carnis]], that is, these legal ceremonies have the appearance of wisdom also because they withdraw many pleasant things from the body, such as pork: hence they seem to belong to sobriety and abstinence; for which reason those who observe them judge those who do not to be gluttons.

3.title: DECLARATIO CAPITULI TERTII : IGITUR SI CONSURREXISTIS, ETC.
3.title_en: Explanation of the third chapter: Therefore, if you be risen, etc.

paras.t: Expleta informatione Apostoli de vitandis legalibus et naturalibus versutiis, jam inducitur moralis instructio. Igitur, id est, quia legalia cessaverunt, et vos cum Christo mortui estis, si consurrexistis a lapsu peccati, cum Christo, id est, sicut Christus surrexit a tumulo. Peccator enim jacet prostratus in vitiis, justus vero stat in virtutibus erectus. Quum autem peccator pœnitentiam agit et confitetur, resurgit per gratiam a propriis malis. Quæ sursum sunt quærite, id est, cœlestia præmia desiderate, et summum bonum semper intendite, illa utique quæ oculus non vidit, nec auris audivit, nec in cor hominis ascenderunt, ubi, id est in quo loco superiori, Christus est in dextera Dei, id est ad dexteram Patris, sedens tanquam omnium judex ac Dominus, juxta illud : Dominus Jesus assumptus est in cœlum, et sedet a dextris Dei. Denique Christus secundum suam divinitatem, sedet, id est consistit, ad dexteram Patris, id est in æqualitate majestatis paternæ ; secundum humanitatem vero assumptam, sedet, id est, corporaliter manet, ad dexteram Dei, id est in bonis potioribus Patris. Omnia enim creata Christo homini sunt subjecta.
paras.en: The Apostle's instruction on avoiding the subtleties of the legal observances and of natural philosophy being completed, moral teaching is now brought in. [[3:1|Therefore|Igitur]], that is, since the legal observances have ceased and you are dead with Christ, [[3:1|if you be risen|si consurrexistis]] from the fall of sin [[3:1|with Christ|cum Christo]], that is, as Christ rose from the tomb. For the sinner lies prostrate in vices, but the just man stands upright in virtues; and when the sinner does penance and confesses, he rises again by grace from his own evils. [[3:1|seek the things that are above|Quæ sursum sunt quærite]], that is, desire the heavenly rewards and always aim at the highest good: those things, namely, which [[1 Cor 2:9|eye hath not seen, nor ear heard: neither hath it entered into the heart of man|oculus non vidit, nec auris audivit, nec in cor hominis ascenderunt]]; [[3:1|where|ubi]], that is, in which higher place, [[3:1|Christ is|Christus est]] [[3:1|at the right hand of God|in dextera Dei]], that is, at the right hand of the Father, [[3:1|sitting|sedens]] as Judge and Lord of all, according to that saying: [[Mark 16:19|the Lord Jesus|Dominus Jesus]] [[Mark 16:19|was taken up into heaven and sitteth on the right hand of God|assumptus est in cœlum, et sedet a dextris Dei]] [the margin reads only "v. 19"; the words are Mark 16:19]. Now Christ according to his divinity sits, that is, abides, at the right hand of the Father, that is, in equality with the Father's majesty; but according to the humanity he assumed he sits, that is, remains bodily, at the right hand of God, that is, among the Father's better goods. For all created things are subject to Christ as man[[Heb 2:8||]].

paras.t: Quæ sursum sunt sapite, id est, spiritualia mentis affectu gustate et corde sincero perpendite, […] id est non carnalia et terrena, ut dicere valeatis cum Isaia : Nomen tuum et memoriale tuum […] Domine, in desiderio animæ meæ ; anima mea desideravit te in nocte, sed et spiritus meus in præcordiis meis. Et cum Psalmista : Quam magna multitudo dulcedinis tuæ, Domine ! Itemque cum Sponsa : Indica mihi, quem diligit anima mea, ubi pascas, ubi cubes in meridie.
paras.en: [[3:2|Mind the things that are above|Quæ sursum sunt sapite]], that is, taste spiritual things with the affection of the mind and weigh them with a sincere heart, […] that is, not carnal and earthly things; so that you may be able to say with Isaias: [[Is 26:8|thy name, and thy remembrance|Nomen tuum et memoriale tuum]] […] O Lord, [[Is 26:8|are the desire of the soul|in desiderio animæ meæ]] [Denis: "are in the desire of my soul"]; [[Is 26:9|My soul hath desired thee in the night: yea, and with my spirit within me|anima mea desideravit te in nocte, sed et spiritus meus in præcordiis meis]]. And with the Psalmist: [[Ps 30:20|O how great is the multitude of thy sweetness, O Lord|Quam magna multitudo dulcedinis tuæ, Domine]]! And again with the Bride: [[Cant 1:6|Shew me, O thou whom my soul loveth, where thou feedest, where thou liest in the midday|Indica mihi, quem diligit anima mea, ubi pascas, ubi cubes in meridie]].

paras.t: Mortui enim estis rebus mundanis ac vanis, id est, in talibus occupari non debetis ; vel, Mortui estis, id est in Baptismo configurati morti Christi ; et vita vestra quam habituri estis in patria, abscondita est, id est reposita et latenter consistens, cum Christo in Deo, id est in Deo Patre, in cujus corde et sinu Christus incomprehensibiliter conquiescit : quoniam nemo novit Filium, nisi Pater. Hæc autem vita æterna, est nostra felicitas, in Deo objectaliter sita, de qua dicit Salvator ad Patrem : Hæc est vita æterna : ut cognoscant te solum Deum verum, etc. Vel sic : Vita vestra, id est vita gratiæ et gloriæ, abscondita, id est ignota, est omnibus viatoribus in Deo, qui eam cognoscit atque causaliter continet. Nemo enim novit utrum dignus sit amore an odio.
paras.en: [[3:3|For you are dead|Mortui enim estis]] to worldly and vain things, that is, you ought not to be taken up with such things; or, [[3:3|you are dead|Mortui estis]], that is, in Baptism made conformable to the death of Christ[[Phil 3:10||]]; [[3:3|and your life|et vita vestra]], which you are to have in the fatherland, [[3:3|is hid|abscondita est]], that is, laid up and abiding hidden, [[3:3|with Christ in God|cum Christo in Deo]], that is, in God the Father, in whose heart and bosom Christ rests incomprehensibly: since [[Matt 11:27|no one knoweth the Son but the Father|nemo novit Filium, nisi Pater]]. Now this eternal life is our happiness, set in God as its object [that is, God himself is what the blessed see and enjoy], of which the Saviour says to the Father: [[John 17:3|this is eternal life: That they may know thee, the only true God|Hæc est vita æterna : ut cognoscant te solum Deum verum]], etc. Or thus: [[3:3|your life|Vita vestra]], that is, the life of grace and of glory, [[3:3|is hid|abscondita]], that is, unknown to all wayfarers, [[3:3|in God|in Deo]], who knows it and holds it as its cause. For no one knows [[Eccles 9:1|whether he be worthy of love, or hatred|utrum dignus sit amore an odio]].

paras.t: Quum autem Christus apparuerit, id est, evidenter innotuerit esse, vita vestra objective, id est vivificator et beatificator vester : quod maxime erit in die extremi judicii, quando in conspectu universorum, Christus electorum suorum vita monstrabitur ; tunc et vos apparebitis cum ipso in gloria, id est, anima et corpore gloriosi eritis, atque cum Christo alta cœlorum penetrabitis, ibi cum eo in cœlesti gloria sine fine mansuri.
paras.en: [[3:4|When Christ shall appear|Quum autem Christus apparuerit]], that is, shall be plainly known to be [[3:4|your life|vita vestra]] as its object, that is, the one who gives you life and beatitude: which will be above all on the day of the last judgment, when in the sight of all Christ will be shown to be the life of his elect; [[3:4|then you also shall appear with him in glory|tunc et vos apparebitis cum ipso in gloria]], that is, you will be glorious in soul and body, and with Christ will pass into the heights of heaven, there to abide with him in heavenly glory without end.

paras.t: Præterea, docet Apostolus quomodo ad hanc beatitudinem valeamus pertingere. Mortificate, id est destruite, ergo, videlicet ut vitam hanc sempiternam mereamini adipisci, membra vestra quæ sunt super terram, id est vitia corporis quæ per membra explentur. Unde quasi exponens quid dixerit membra, adjecit : fornicationem, id est concubitum soluti cum soluta, immunditiam, id est peccata contra naturam, libidinem, id est ardorem quemlibet in his quæ ad turpitudinem pertinent, concupiscentiam malam, id est interiorum inclinationem ad vitia carnis, et avaritiam, quæ est idolorum servitus, id est, idololatriæ comparatur : nam sicut idololatra potius servit idolo quam vero Deo, ita avarus magis colit, curat et cogitat suam pecuniam, quam Creatorem.
paras.en: Next the Apostle teaches how we may attain to this beatitude. [[3:5|Mortify|Mortificate]], that is, destroy, [[3:5|therefore|ergo]], namely so that you may deserve to gain this everlasting life, [[3:5|your members which are upon the earth|membra vestra quæ sunt super terram]], that is, the vices of the body which are carried out through the members. Hence, as though explaining what he meant by members, he added: [[3:5|fornication|fornicationem]][[Eph 5:3||]], that is, the intercourse of an unmarried man with an unmarried woman; [[3:5|uncleanness|immunditiam]], that is, sins against nature; [[3:5|lust|libidinem]], that is, any burning in the things that belong to shamefulness; [[3:5|evil concupiscence|concupiscentiam malam]], that is, the inclination of the inner powers to the vices of the flesh; [[3:5|and covetousness, which is the service of idols|et avaritiam, quæ est idolorum servitus]], that is, it is likened to idolatry: for as the idolater serves an idol rather than the true God, so the covetous man worships, cares for and thinks of his money more than of the Creator.

paras.t: Propter quæ vitia venit ira Dei, id est divinæ justitiæ ultio, super filios incredulitatis, id est in homines infideles ac reprobos ; in quibus peccatis et vos, Colossenses, ambulastis, id est conversati estis, aliquando, eundo de malo in pejus, quum viveretis in illis, quando videlicet nondum conversi fuistis ad Christum.
paras.en: [[3:6|For which things|Propter quæ]] vices [[3:6|the wrath of God cometh|venit ira Dei]], that is, the vengeance of divine justice, [[3:6|upon the children of unbelief|super filios incredulitatis]], that is, upon unbelieving and reprobate men; [[3:7|In which|in quibus]] sins [[3:7|you also|et vos]], Colossians, [[3:7|walked|ambulastis]], that is, lived, [[3:7|some time|aliquando]], going from bad to worse, [[3:7|when you lived in them|quum viveretis in illis]], that is, when you had not yet been converted to Christ.

paras.t: Nunc autem deponite et vos omnia quæ sequuntur, videlicet : iram, quæ inordinatus appetitus est vindictæ propter parvipensionem, indignationem, quæ ex superbia et ira procedit, malitiam, id est machinationem mali in alium corde conceptam, blasphemiam contra Deum et Sanctos, turpem, id est impudicum, sermonem deponite de ore vestro. Nolite mentiri invicem. Os enim quod mentitur, occidit animam, ut dicitur in libro Sapientiæ.
paras.en: [[3:8|But now put you also all away|Nunc autem deponite et vos omnia]] that follow, namely: [[3:8|anger|iram]], which is an inordinate desire of revenge for a slight; [[3:8|indignation|indignationem]], which proceeds from pride and anger; [[3:8|malice|malitiam]], that is, the plotting of evil against another conceived in the heart; [[3:8|blasphemy|blasphemiam]] against God and the Saints; [[3:8|filthy|turpem]], that is, unchaste, [[3:8|speech|sermonem]]: put these away [[3:8|out of your mouth|de ore vestro]]. [[3:9|Lie not one to another|Nolite mentiri invicem]]. For [[Wis 1:11|the mouth that belieth, killeth the soul|Os enim quod mentitur, occidit animam]], as is said in the book of Wisdom.

paras.t: Exspoliantes vos, id est exuentes, veterem hominem, id est pristinum statum, vel vosmetipsos quoad id quod fuistis per culpam, cum actibus suis vitiosis ; et induentes novum, id est, per opera bona ac sacramenta et gratiam, induite hominem spiritualiter reformatum, id est, vos ipsos innovate interius, qui novus homo renovatur et crescit quotidie in agnitionem Dei, id est contemplando divina. Renovatur autem hoc modo : secundum imaginem ejus, id est quantum ad partem intellectivam, in qua est imago ejus qui fecit eum, id est summi Creatoris, cujus imago resplendet in superiori parte animæ rationalis : quæ pars potestativa renovatur quotidie recipiendo a Deo gratiæ incrementa, ornamenta virtutum et sapientiæ claritatem.
paras.en: [[3:9|stripping yourselves|Exspoliantes vos]], that is, putting off, [[3:9|of the old man|veterem hominem]], that is, your former state, or yourselves as to what you were through sin, [[3:9|with his deeds|cum actibus suis]] of vice; [[3:10|And putting on the new|et induentes novum]], that is, through good works, the sacraments and grace put on the man spiritually re-formed, that is, renew yourselves inwardly; [[3:10|him who|qui]], the new man, [[3:10|is renewed|renovatur]] and grows daily [[3:10|unto knowledge|in agnitionem]] of God, that is, by contemplating divine things. And he is renewed in this way: [[3:10|according to the image of him|secundum imaginem ejus]], that is, as to the intellectual part, in which is the image [[3:10|of him that created him|ejus qui fecit eum]], that is, of the supreme Creator, whose image shines forth in the higher part of the rational soul; and this power of the soul is renewed daily by receiving from God increases of grace, the adornments of the virtues and the brightness of wisdom.

paras.t: Ubi, id est in quo homine interiori ac novo, videlicet in parte animæ intellectiva, non est masculus neque fœmina, id est discretio sexus, quæ attenditur secundum corpus, non animam ; nec est ibi gentilis et Judæus, id est discretio generis, quoniam omnes quantum ad animam, immediate a Deo creantur, circumcisio et præputium, id est differentia observationis seu ritus, Barbarus et Scytha, id est differentia linguarum, servus et liber, id est distinctio conditionis. Est itaque sensus, quod propter ista non est unus dignior vel indignior coram Deo. Nam quantum ad hominem interiorem, nulla diversitas exterior sexuum, nationum, observationum, linguarum aut conditionum, præjudicat alteri. Sed omnia et in omnibus Christus, id est, Christus est omnia causaliter, omnibus generibus atque operibus hominum dans exsistentiam ac permanentiam. Ipse quoque in omnibus est per gratiam vel providentiam.
paras.en: [[3:11|Where|Ubi]], that is, in which inner and new man, namely in the intellectual part of the soul, [[3:11|there is neither|non est]] male nor female [Denis adds these words, from Gal 3:28, to the verse], that is, distinction of sex, which is reckoned according to the body, not the soul; nor is there in it [[3:11|Gentile nor Jew|gentilis et Judæus]], that is, distinction of race, since all, as to the soul, are created immediately by God; [[3:11|circumcision nor uncircumcision|circumcisio et præputium]], that is, difference of observance or rite; [[3:11|Barbarian nor Scythian|Barbarus et Scytha]], that is, difference of tongues; [[3:11|bond nor free|servus et liber]], that is, distinction of condition. So the sense is that on account of these things one is not more worthy or less worthy than another before God. For as to the inner man, no outward diversity of sex, nation, observance, tongue or condition prejudices one against another. [[3:11|But Christ is all and in all|Sed omnia et in omnibus Christus]], that is, Christ is all things as their cause, giving existence and continuance to all kinds of men and to all their works. He is also in all things by grace or by providence.

paras.t: Induite ergo vos sicut electi Dei, id est a Deo prædestinati, ut speramus vel Deo revelante cognoscimus, sancti, id est a vitiis emundati per sacramenta Ecclesiæ, et dilecti a Deo, recipiendo beneficia ejus, viscera misericordiæ, id est internos pietatis affectus, benignitatem, id est animi præparationem ad benefaciendum proximis vel ipsum misericordiæ opus, humilitatem, modestiam, id est moderamen in verbis ac factis, patientiam.
paras.en: [[3:12|Put ye on therefore, as the elect of God|Induite ergo vos sicut electi Dei]], that is, predestined by God, as we hope, or know by God's revealing it, [[3:12|holy|sancti]], that is, cleansed from vices through the sacraments of the Church, [[3:12|and beloved|et dilecti]] by God, in receiving his benefits, [[3:12|the bowels of mercy|viscera misericordiæ]], that is, inward affections of pity; [[3:12|benignity|benignitatem]], that is, readiness of mind to do good to our neighbours, or the very work of mercy; [[3:12|humility, modesty|humilitatem, modestiam]], that is, moderation in words and deeds; [[3:12|patience|patientiam]].

paras.t: Supportantes invicem : sicut Galatis dictum est, Alter alterius onera portate ; et item Romanis, Debemus nos firmiores, imbecillitates infirmorum sustinere : et donantes vobismetipsis, id est mutuo ignoscentes, si quis adversus aliquem habet querelam, id est, si unus vestrum ab alio est offensus, seu injuriam passus. Sicut et Dominus Christus seu Trinitas donavit, id est, indulsit pure, gratis et festinanter, vobis, ita et vos vestris debitoribus indulgete. Unde dicit Salvator : Exemplum dedi vobis, ut quemadmodum ego feci vobis, ita et vos faciatis ; alibi quoque, Si non dimiseritis de cordibus vestris, nec Pater vester dimittet vobis peccata vestra. Denique quam enorme sit ita non agere, constat per ea quæ in Ecclesiastico scribuntur : Homo homini servat iram, et a Deo quærit medelam ? In hominem sibi similem non habet misericordiam, et de peccatis suis deprecatur Altissimum ? Quis exorabit pro peccatis illius ?
paras.en: [[3:13|Bearing with one another|Supportantes invicem]]: as was said to the Galatians, [[Gal 6:2|Bear ye one another's burdens|Alter alterius onera portate]]; and again to the Romans, [[Rom 15:1|we that are stronger ought to bear the infirmities of the weak|Debemus nos firmiores, imbecillitates infirmorum sustinere]]; [[3:13|and forgiving one another|et donantes vobismetipsis]], that is, pardoning each other, [[3:13|if any have a complaint against another|si quis adversus aliquem habet querelam]], that is, if one of you has been offended by another, or suffered a wrong. [[3:13|Even as the Lord|Sicut et Dominus]] Christ, or the Trinity, [[3:13|hath forgiven|donavit]], that is, has pardoned purely, freely and speedily, you, [[3:13|so do you also|ita et vos]] forgive your debtors [Denis's text adds these words to the verse]. Hence the Saviour says: [[John 13:15|I have given you an example, that as I have done to you, so you do also|Exemplum dedi vobis, ut quemadmodum ego feci vobis, ita et vos faciatis]]; and elsewhere too, [[Matt 18:35|if you forgive not every one his brother from your hearts|Si non dimiseritis de cordibus vestris]], [[Matt 6:15|neither will your Father forgive you your offences|nec Pater vester dimittet vobis peccata vestra]] [no margin reference; Denis joins Matt 18:35 with Matt 6:15 (or Mark 11:26)]. Lastly, how monstrous it is not to do so is clear from what is written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 28:3|Man to man reserveth anger, and doth he seek remedy of God?|Homo homini servat iram, et a Deo quærit medelam]] [[Ecclus 28:4|He hath no mercy on a man like himself, and doth he entreat for his own sins?|In hominem sibi similem non habet misericordiam, et de peccatis suis deprecatur Altissimum]] [Denis adds "the Most High"] [[Ecclus 28:5|who shall obtain pardon for his sins|Quis exorabit pro peccatis illius]]?

paras.t: Super omnia autem hæc, caritatem habete, id est, hoc præ ceteris omnibus hortor, et summe necessarium utilissimumque est, ut caritatem Dei et proximi habeatis. Propter quod ait Salvator : Mandatum novum do vobis, ut diligatis invicem. Quam, id est quam caritatem habere, est vinculum perfectionis, id est aliarum virtutum conservatio, consummatio, nexus ac ligamentum. Caritas enim est præstantissima virtus, omnes virtutes movens, perficiens et meritorias reddens : qua subtracta, nulla virtus meritoria permanet. Propterea beatissimus Archiapostolus in prima sua Canonica : Ante omnia, inquit, mutuam in vobis caritatem continuam habentes, quoniam caritas operit multitudinem peccatorum.
paras.en: [[3:14|But above all these things have charity|Super omnia autem hæc, caritatem habete]], that is, this I urge before all else, and it is supremely necessary and most profitable, that you have charity toward God and your neighbour. For this reason the Saviour says: [[John 13:34|A new commandment I give unto you: That you love one another|Mandatum novum do vobis, ut diligatis invicem]]. [[3:14|which|Quam]], that is, to have which charity, [[3:14|is the bond of perfection|est vinculum perfectionis]], that is, the preserving, the consummation, the knot and the binding of the other virtues. For charity is the most excellent virtue, moving all the virtues, perfecting them and making them meritorious: take it away, and no virtue remains meritorious. Therefore the most blessed chief Apostle [Denis's word is Archiapostolus, that is, Peter] says in his first Canonical Epistle: [[1 Pet 4:8|before all things|Ante omnia]], he says, [[1 Pet 4:8|have a constant mutual charity among yourselves: for charity covereth a multitude of sins|mutuam in vobis caritatem continuam habentes, quoniam caritas operit multitudinem peccatorum]].

paras.t: Et pax Christi, id est interna et vera pax, scilicet tranquillitas cordis, seu quies mentis in Deo, exsultet, id est, redundantem lætitiam pariat, in cordibus vestris. Pace enim quid dulcius, quidve jucundius esse potest ? In qua pace et vocati estis in uno corpore mystico : id est, per pacem positi estis inter membra Christi ; imo ad hoc vocati estis in unam Ecclesiam, ut sempiternam sortiamini pacem. Unde dictum est alibi : In pace vocavit nos Dominus. Et grates estote Deo pro universis beneficiis ejus. Qui enim gratus agit, dona potioribus meretur implere, juxta illud in Evangelio : Omni habenti dabitur, id est grato.
paras.en: [[3:15|And let the peace of Christ|Et pax Christi]], that is, inward and true peace, namely tranquillity of heart or the rest of the mind in God, [[3:15|rejoice|exsultet]], that is, bring forth overflowing gladness, [[3:15|in your hearts|in cordibus vestris]]. For what can be sweeter or more delightful than peace? [[3:15|wherein|In qua]] peace [[3:15|also you are called in one body|et vocati estis in uno corpore]], the mystical body: that is, through peace you have been set among the members of Christ; nay, you have been called into the one Church for this, that you may obtain everlasting peace. Hence it is said elsewhere: [[1 Cor 7:15|God hath called us in peace|In pace vocavit nos Dominus]] [Denis has "the Lord" for "God"]. [[3:15|and be ye thankful|Et grates estote]] to God for all his benefits. For he who acts with gratitude deserves to be filled with better gifts, according to that saying in the Gospel: [[Matt 25:29|to every one that hath shall be given|Omni habenti dabitur]], that is, to the grateful.

paras.t: Verbum Christi, id est evangelica doctrina ex ore Christi prolata, habitet, id est stabiliter maneat, in vobis, id est in mentibus vestris per jugem memoriam et veram obedientiam : juxta illud in Psalmo, In corde meo abscondi eloquia tua, ut non peccem tibi. […] est intellectu sapientiali totius Scripturæ sacræ, quatenus verba Christi sapienter intelligatis, docentes et commonentes, id est exhortantes, vosmetipsos ad opera perfectiora, in psalmis, qui ad bonam operationem hortantur, et hymnis, in quibus divina laus continetur, et canticis spiritualibus, quæ de cœlestibus bonis futurisque gaudiis agunt ; in gratia gratificante, sine qua nihil est meritorium ; vel, In gratia, id est cum gratiarum actione ; vel, In gratia, id est consideratione gratuitorum beneficiorum Dei ; cantantes, id est laudem dicentes, in cordibus vestris, id est cordiali affectu et cum mentali attentione, Deo : quemadmodum scriptum est, Laudabit usque ad mortem anima mea Dominum ; et in Psalmo, Cantabo Domino in vita mea, psallam Deo meo quamdiu sum. Hoc dicitur contra eos qui non corde, sed labiis Deum glorificant : de quibus per Isaiam Dominus contestatur, Appropinquat populus iste ore suo, et labiis glorificat me, cor autem ejus longe est a me.
paras.en: [[3:16|Let the word of Christ|Verbum Christi]], that is, the gospel teaching uttered by the mouth of Christ, [[3:16|dwell|habitet]], that is, abide steadfastly, [[3:16|in you|in vobis]], that is, in your minds, by constant remembrance and true obedience: according to that saying in the Psalm, [[Ps 118:11|Thy words have I hidden in my heart, that I may not sin against thee|In corde meo abscondi eloquia tua, ut non peccem tibi]]. […] is, with a wise understanding of the whole of Holy Scripture, so that you may understand the words of Christ wisely; [[3:16|teaching and admonishing|docentes et commonentes]], that is, exhorting, [[3:16|one another|vosmetipsos]] to more perfect works, [[3:16|in psalms|in psalmis]], which exhort to good action, [[3:16|hymns|et hymnis]], in which the praise of God is contained, [[3:16|and spiritual canticles|et canticis spiritualibus]], which treat of heavenly goods and the joys to come; [[3:16|in grace|in gratia]], sanctifying grace [gratia gratificans, the grace that makes us pleasing to God], without which nothing is meritorious; or, [[3:16|in grace|In gratia]], that is, with thanksgiving; or, [[3:16|in grace|In gratia]], that is, in consideration of the free benefits of God; [[3:16|singing|cantantes]], that is, uttering praise, [[3:16|in your hearts|in cordibus vestris]], that is, with heartfelt affection and with the attention of the mind, [[3:16|to God|Deo]]: as it is written, [[Ecclus 51:8|My soul shall praise the Lord even to death|Laudabit usque ad mortem anima mea Dominum]] [the margin gives Eccli. ii, 8; the words are Ecclus 51:8]; and in the Psalm, [[Ps 103:33|I will sing to the Lord as long as I live: I will sing praise to my God while I have my being|Cantabo Domino in vita mea, psallam Deo meo quamdiu sum]]. This is said against those who glorify God not with the heart but with the lips, of whom the Lord protests through Isaias: [[Is 29:13|this people draw near me with their mouth, and with their lips glorify me, but their heart is far from me|Appropinquat populus iste ore suo, et labiis glorificat me, cor autem ejus longe est a me]].

paras.t: Omne quodcumque facitis in verbo, id est prædicando, docendo, hortando, orando, cantando, aut in opere exteriori, omnia in nomine Domini nostri Jesu Christi, id est ad gloriam Christi, et cum invocatione nominis ejus, facite, gratias agentes Deo et Patri, id est sanctæ Trinitati, cui quotidie dicimus : Pater noster, qui es in cœlis ; per ipsum, id est ex consideratione beneficiorum quæ Trinitas nobis largita est per mediatorem nostrum hominem Christum.
paras.en: [[3:17|All whatsoever you do in word|Omne quodcumque facitis in verbo]], that is, in preaching, teaching, exhorting, praying, singing, [[3:17|or in work|aut in opere]] outwardly, [[3:17|do all in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ|omnia in nomine Domini nostri Jesu Christi]], that is, for the glory of Christ and with the invocation of his name, [[3:17|giving thanks to God and the Father|gratias agentes Deo et Patri]], that is, to the Holy Trinity, to whom we say daily: [[Matt 6:9|Our Father who art in heaven|Pater noster, qui es in cœlis]]; [[3:17|by him|per ipsum]], that is, from consideration of the benefits which the Trinity has bestowed on us through our mediator, the man Christ[[1 Tim 2:5||]].

paras.t: Præterea descendit Apostolus ad moralem particularium personarum instructionem. Mulieres, subditæ estote viris, id est maritis vestris, sicut oportet in Domino, id est, sicut Deus instituit, dicens mulieri : Sub viri potestate eris, et ipse dominabitur tui. Vel, Sicut oportet in Domino, id est in licitis et honestis quæ complacent Deo.
paras.en: Next the Apostle comes down to moral instruction for particular persons. [[3:18|Wives, be subject to your husbands|Mulieres, subditæ estote viris]], that is, to your married husbands, [[3:18|as it behoveth in the Lord|sicut oportet in Domino]], that is, as God ordained, saying to the woman: [[Gen 3:16|thou shalt be under thy husband's power, and he shall have dominion over thee|Sub viri potestate eris, et ipse dominabitur tui]]. Or, [[3:18|as it behoveth in the Lord|Sicut oportet in Domino]], that is, in lawful and honest things that are pleasing to God.

paras.t: Viri, diligite uxores vestras, non solum maritali et naturali affectu, sed spirituali dilectione, et nolite amari esse ad illas, sed secundum scientiam cohabitate illis, tanquam infirmioribus vasculis impertientes honorem. Unde in Ecclesiastico habetur : Noli esse sicut leo in domo tua, evertens domesticos tuos, et opprimens tibi subjectos.
paras.en: [[3:19|Husbands, love your wives|Viri, diligite uxores vestras]], not only with married and natural affection but with spiritual love, [[3:19|and be not bitter towards them|et nolite amari esse ad illas]], but dwell with them according to knowledge, giving them honour as to weaker vessels[[1 Pet 3:7||]]. Hence it is said in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 4:35|Be not as a lion in thy house, terrifying them of thy household, and oppressing them that are under thee|Noli esse sicut leo in domo tua, evertens domesticos tuos, et opprimens tibi subjectos]].

paras.t: Filii, obedite parentibus per omnia quæ sunt apta materia obedientiæ, id est in cunctis bonis ac licitis, et majus bonum non impedientibus. Hoc enim placitum est in Domino. Nam Deus hoc jussit. Patres, nolite ad indignationem provocare filios vestros, habendo vos indiscrete et non paterne ad eos, ut non pusillo animo fiant, id est, ne per pusillanimitatem frangantur, et obedire desistant, non valentes ferre duritiam vestram. Omnia hæc ad spirituales patres eorumque filios maxime pertinent.
paras.en: [[3:20|Children, obey your parents in all things|Filii, obedite parentibus per omnia]] that are fit matter for obedience, that is, in all things good and lawful that do not hinder a greater good. [[3:20|for this is well pleasing to the Lord|Hoc enim placitum est in Domino]]. For God commanded it[[Ex 20:12||]]. [[3:21|Fathers, provoke not your children to indignation|Patres, nolite ad indignationem provocare filios vestros]] by behaving towards them without discretion and not as fathers, [[3:21|lest they be discouraged|ut non pusillo animo fiant]], that is, lest they be broken by faintheartedness and give up obeying, unable to bear your harshness. All these things apply above all to spiritual fathers and their sons.

paras.t: Servi, obedite per omnia, id est in omnibus bonis, dominis carnalibus, id est temporalibus, in corporalibus dominationem exercentibus ; non ad oculum servientes, id est non solo servili timore et in dominorum vestrorum præsentia, quasi hominibus placentes, id est tanquam hoc solum optantes et intendentes, ut hominibus placeatis, et non potius Deo, sed in simplicitate cordis, id est, sincera intentione servite dominis illis carnalibus, etiam dyscolis, timentes Deum casto ac filiali timore, cujus præsentiam seu conspectum non potestis effugere.
paras.en: [[3:22|Servants, obey in all things|Servi, obedite per omnia]], that is, in all good things, [[3:22|your masters according to the flesh|dominis carnalibus]], that is, your temporal masters, who exercise lordship in bodily matters; [[3:22|not serving to the eye|non ad oculum servientes]], that is, not only from servile fear and in your masters' presence, [[3:22|as pleasing men|quasi hominibus placentes]], that is, as wishing and aiming only at this, to please men and not rather God; [[3:22|but in simplicity of heart|sed in simplicitate cordis]], that is, serve those masters according to the flesh with a sincere intention, even the froward[[1 Pet 2:18||]], [[3:22|fearing God|timentes Deum]] with a chaste and filial fear, whose presence or sight you cannot escape.

paras.t: Quodcumque facietis in obsequio dominorum vestrorum, ex animo, id est cum promptitudine voluntatis, operamini, utpote amore justitiæ atque intuitu mercedis divinæ, non timore pœnæ et solo intuitu remunerationis humanæ : talem enim animam approbat Deus ; sicut Domino Deo principaliter servientes, et non hominibus tantum : quia etsi hominibus deservitis, hoc tamen propter Deum libenter facere debetis, quasi sustinentes hanc servitutem ex ordinatione divina, pro pœna peccati cui obnoxii estis. Servitus nempe ob culpam inducta est.
paras.en: [[3:23|Whatsoever you do|Quodcumque facietis]] in the service of your masters, [[3:23|from the heart|ex animo]], that is, with readiness of will, [[3:23|do it|operamini]]: that is, out of love of justice and with an eye to the divine reward, not from fear of punishment and with an eye only to human recompense, for such a soul God approves; [[3:23|as to the Lord|sicut Domino]] God, serving him first of all, [[3:23|and not to men|et non hominibus]] only: for although you serve men, you ought to do it willingly for God's sake, as bearing this servitude by divine ordinance[[Rom 13:1||]], as the punishment of the sin to which you are liable. For servitude was brought in on account of sin.

paras.t: Scientes fide certissima, quod a Domino accipietis retributionem hereditatis, id est præmium vitæ æternæ, quæ est hereditas electorum. Retributio autem hereditatis aliud non est nisi ipsa hereditas quæ donatur. Hanc hereditatem habebitis, si præfato modo servientes fueritis. Domino Jesu Christo servite summe atque finaliter, imo et latriæ servitute, quæ soli Deo debetur.
paras.en: [[3:24|Knowing|Scientes]] by most certain faith [[3:24|that you shall receive of the Lord the reward of inheritance|quod a Domino accipietis retributionem hereditatis]], that is, the reward of eternal life, which is the inheritance of the elect. And the reward of inheritance is nothing other than the inheritance itself which is given. This inheritance you will have if you have served in the way just described. [[3:24|Serve ye the Lord Christ|Domino Jesu Christo servite]] [Denis reads "the Lord Jesus Christ"] supremely and as your last end, nay, with the service of latria [that is, the worship due to God alone], which is owed to God alone.

paras.t: Qui enim injuriam facit alteri, infideliter serviendo, aut alio modo, recipiet id quod inique gessit, id est, pro sua injustitia debitam pœnam exsolvet, juxta illud Psalmistæ : Qui custodit veritatem in sæculum, facit judicium injuriam patientibus ; et alibi, Mihi vindictam, et ego retribuam, dicit Dominus. Et non est personarum acceptio apud Deum. Hoc jam ubertim dictum atque expositum est. Deus enim neminem ad se venientem, vel quod in se est facientem, repellit ; nullius etiam peccata inulta dimittit. Unde ipse Dominus in Joanne testatur : Eum qui venit ad me, non ejiciam foras. Et alibi ait Scriptura : Deus opus hominis reddet ei, et juxta vias singulorum restituet ; itemque, Si direxerit homo ad Deum cor suum, spiritum illius et flatum ad se trahet. Ex his tamen non sequitur, quin Deus justus ac sapiens ab æterno elegerit unum præ alio, etiam absque omni merito hominum.
paras.en: [[3:25|For he that doth wrong|Qui enim injuriam facit]] to another, by serving unfaithfully or in any other way, [[3:25|shall receive for that which he hath done wrongfully|recipiet id quod inique gessit]], that is, shall pay the penalty due for his injustice: according to that saying of the Psalmist, [[Ps 145:7|Who keepeth truth for ever: who executeth judgment for them that suffer wrong|Qui custodit veritatem in sæculum, facit judicium injuriam patientibus]]; and elsewhere, [[Rom 12:19|Revenge is mine, I will repay, saith the Lord|Mihi vindictam, et ego retribuam, dicit Dominus]]. [[3:25|And there is no respect of persons with God|Et non est personarum acceptio apud Deum]]. This has already been said and explained at length. For God repels no one who comes to him, or who does what lies in him [that is, who does all he can with the grace given him]; nor does he leave anyone's sins unpunished. Hence the Lord himself testifies in John: [[John 6:37|him that cometh to me, I will not cast out|Eum qui venit ad me, non ejiciam foras]]. And elsewhere Scripture says: God [[Job 34:11|will render to a man his work, and according to the ways of every one he will reward them|opus hominis reddet ei, et juxta vias singulorum restituet]]; and again, [[Job 34:14|If he turn his heart to him, he shall draw his spirit and breath unto himself|Si direxerit homo ad Deum cor suum, spiritum illius et flatum ad se trahet]]. Yet it does not follow from these things that God, just and wise, did not choose one before another from eternity, even without any merit of men.

paras.t: Domini, quod justum est ratione obsequii vobis exhibiti, et æquum propter conformitatem naturæ in vobis ac servis, servis vestris præstate, videlicet dignam mercedem et piam subventionem ac miserationem ; scientes quoniam et vos Dominum justum ac infallibilem judicem habetis in cælo, qui eadem mensura qua mensi fueritis, remetietur vobis. Sic enim facit homini, quemadmodum homo proximo suo.
paras.en: [[Col 4:1|Masters|Domini]], [[Col 4:1|that which is just|quod justum est]] by reason of the service rendered to you, [[Col 4:1|and equal|et æquum]] because of the likeness of nature in you and in your servants, [[Col 4:1|do to your servants|servis vestris præstate]], namely a fitting wage and kindly help and compassion; [[Col 4:1|knowing that you also have a master|scientes quoniam et vos Dominum]], a just and infallible judge, [[Col 4:1|in heaven|in cælo]], who will requite you, for [[Luke 6:38|with the same measure that you shall mete withal, it shall be measured to you again|eadem mensura qua mensi fueritis, remetietur vobis]]. For he does to a man as that man does to his neighbour.

4.title: EXPLANATIO CAPITULI QUARTI : ORATIONI INSTATE, VIGILANTES IN EA.
4.title_en: Explanation of the fourth chapter: Be instant in prayer, watching in it.

paras.t: REDIT Apostolus ad generalem exhortationem, seque discipulorum suorum precibus commendat. Orationi pro vobis ac aliis fusæ instate, id est, instanter seu diligenter ac perseveranter intendite, vigilantes, id est vigili mente durantes, imo et pernoctantes in ea, exemplo Christi, de quo scriptum est in Evangelio : Erat Jesus pernoctans in oratione Dei. Indesinenter ergo, vigilanter et affectuose orandum est. Propter quod ait Salvator : Oportet semper orare, et non deficere. In Ecclesiastico quoque scriptum legitur : Non impediaris orare semper; et, Ante orationem præpara animam tuam. Denique libenter vacare nos convenit orationi, pensantes illud Chrysostomi : Considera quanta tibi concessa est felicitas, quanta gloria attributa, orationibus fabulari cum Deo, cum Christo miscere colloquia, optare quod velis, quod desideras postulare. Dicit quoque Chrysostomus, quod orans in conventu vel in publico, nil novi facere debet quod adspiciant alii, vel clamando, vel pectus percutiendo, vel manus extendendo. Sic ergo orationi instate, vigilantes in ea in gratiarum actione, id est, orationi gratiarum actionem de præteritis bonis miscete, quia hoc plurimum confert ad obtinendum quod petitur. Nam et dilectionem accendit, benevolentiam captat, et ad potiora disponit.
paras.en: The Apostle returns to general exhortation, and commends himself to the prayers of his disciples. [[4:2|Be instant in prayer|orationi instate]], poured forth for yourselves and for others; that is, apply yourselves to it instantly, or diligently and perseveringly; [[4:2|watching|vigilantes]], that is, continuing with a wakeful mind, and even passing the night [[4:2|in it|in ea]], after the example of Christ, of whom it is written in the Gospel: [[Luke 6:12|he passed the whole night in the prayer of God|Erat Jesus pernoctans in oratione Dei]]. We must pray, then, unceasingly, watchfully and with affection. For which reason the Saviour says: [[Luke 18:1|we ought always to pray and not to faint|Oportet semper orare, et non deficere]]. In Ecclesiasticus too we read it written: [[Ecclus 18:22|Let nothing hinder thee from praying always|Non impediaris orare semper]]; and, [[Ecclus 18:23|Before prayer prepare thy soul|Ante orationem præpara animam tuam]]. Lastly, it befits us to give ourselves willingly to prayer, weighing that saying of Chrysostom: Consider how great a happiness has been granted thee, how great a glory bestowed, to converse with God in prayer, to hold talk with Christ, to ask for what thou wilt, to beg for what thou desirest. Chrysostom says also that one who prays in an assembly or in public ought to do nothing out of the ordinary for others to look at, whether by crying out, or beating the breast, or stretching out the hands. Be instant, then, in prayer, watching in it [[4:2|with thanksgiving|in gratiarum actione]]; that is, mingle with your prayer thanksgiving for past benefits, for this helps very much toward obtaining what is asked. For it both kindles love, wins goodwill, and disposes us for greater things.

paras.t: Orantes simul et pro nobis, ut Deus aperiat nobis ostium sermonis, id est, os meum seu labia unde verba egrediuntur velut ex janua, ipse aperiat (sicut ait Psalmista : Domine, labia mea aperies), hoc est, ut Deus gratiam menti meæ infundat, per quam ad loquendum divinitus movear, et non tam ego loquar, quam Spiritus Sanctus per me : prout in libro Regum David aiebat, Spiritus Domini locutus est per me, et sermo ejus per linguam meam; ad loquendum mysterium Christi, id est ad prædicandum divina secreta de Christo, videlicet incarnationem, passionem, ascensionem, etc. Ex iis constat, quod nemo nostrum adeo perfectus seu virtuosus esse debet in oculis suis, ut non curet orationis suffragium etiam ab inferioribus flagitare, quum videat sacratissimum istum divinissimumque Apostolum tam frequenter atque humiliter pro se orari efflagitare. Propter quod prædicationis officium etiam vinctus sum jam apud Ephesum. Unde patet Apostolum hanc scripsisse epistolam de carcere Ephesi. — Aperiat, inquam, mihi Dominus ostium sermonis, ut manifestem illud, id est, prædictum Christi mysterium clare enuntiem et exponam, ut consequar præmium sempiternum, quemadmodum Sapientia ipsa loquitur : Qui elucidant me, vitam æternam habebunt; ita, id est tam efficaciter et constanter, ut oportet me loqui, id est aliis intimare mysteria Christi propter gratiam apostolatus mihi concessam.
paras.en: [[4:3|Praying withal for us also, that God may open unto us a door of speech|Orantes simul et pro nobis, ut Deus aperiat nobis ostium sermonis]], that is, that He Himself may open my mouth, or the lips from which words go forth as from a door (as the Psalmist says: [[Ps 50:17|O Lord, thou wilt open my lips|Domine, labia mea aperies]]); that is, that God may pour into my mind the grace by which I may be moved from on high to speak, so that it is not so much I who speak as the Holy Ghost through me: as David said in the book of Kings, [[2 Kings 23:2|The spirit of the Lord hath spoken by me and his word by my tongue|Spiritus Domini locutus est per me, et sermo ejus per linguam meam]]; [[4:3|to speak the mystery of Christ|ad loquendum mysterium Christi]], that is, to preach the divine secrets concerning Christ, namely the incarnation, the passion, the ascension, etc. From this it is clear that none of us ought to be so perfect or virtuous in his own eyes as not to care to beg the help of prayer even from his inferiors, seeing that this most holy and most divine Apostle so often and so humbly begs to be prayed for. [[4:3|for which also I am bound|propter quod etiam vinctus sum]], that is, on account of the office of preaching, I am now in bonds at Ephesus. Hence it is plain that the Apostle wrote this epistle from prison at Ephesus. — May the Lord, I say, open to me the door of speech, [[4:4|That I may make it manifest|ut manifestem illud]], that is, that I may clearly declare and set forth the aforesaid mystery of Christ, so as to attain the everlasting reward, as Wisdom herself says: [[Ecclus 24:31|They that explain me shall have life everlasting|Qui elucidant me, vitam æternam habebunt]]; [[4:4|as|ita]], that is, as effectually and constantly, [[4:4|I ought to speak|ut oportet me loqui]], that is, to make known to others the mysteries of Christ, by reason of the grace of the apostleship granted to me.

paras.t: Consequenter admonet eos ad conversationem exemplarem. In sapientia ambulate ad eos, id est, prudenter et exemplariter vivite coram illis, qui foris sunt, qui ad Christi gregem et Ecclesiæ unitatem non pertinent, vel coram quibuscumque extraneis et ignotis, ne scandalizentur. Unde alio loco docet Apostolus : Honeste ambuletis ad eos qui foris sunt; et Christus in Evangelio, Luceat lux vestra coram hominibus. Patet ergo quod secundum Apostolum, curandum est nobis de fama honesta, non ob propriam laudem, sed ad Dei honorem et proximorum salutem. Propter quod apud Ecclesiasten legitur : Melius est nomen bonum quam unguenta pretiosa; et alibi : Curam habe de bono nomine; hoc enim magis proderit tibi quam mille thesauri. Hinc etiam inverecundo et de inhonesto nomine non curanti, dictum est per Jeremiam : Frons mulieris meretricis facta est tibi, noluisti erubescere. Tempus redimentes, id est fructuose expendentes.
paras.en: Next he urges them to an exemplary manner of life. [[4:5|Walk with wisdom towards them|In sapientia ambulate ad eos]], that is, live prudently and as an example before those [[4:5|that are without|qui foris sunt]], who do not belong to Christ's flock and the unity of the Church, or before any strangers and persons unknown, lest they be scandalized. Hence the Apostle teaches in another place: [[1 Thess 4:11|that you walk honestly towards them that are without|Honeste ambuletis ad eos qui foris sunt]] [the margin gives 1 Thess. iv, 11; in modern numbering the words are at 4:12]; and Christ in the Gospel: [[Matt 5:16|let your light shine before men|Luceat lux vestra coram hominibus]]. It is plain, then, that according to the Apostle we must take care of a good reputation, not for our own praise, but for the honour of God and the salvation of our neighbours. For which reason we read in Ecclesiastes: [[Eccles 7:2|A good name is better than precious ointments|Melius est nomen bonum quam unguenta pretiosa]]; and elsewhere: [[Ecclus 41:15|Take care of a good name: for this shall continue with thee, more than a thousand treasures|Curam habe de bono nomine; hoc enim magis proderit tibi quam mille thesauri]]. Hence too it was said through Jeremias to one shameless and careless of a dishonourable name: [[Jer 3:3|thou hadst a harlot's forehead, thou wouldst not blush|Frons mulieris meretricis facta est tibi, noluisti erubescere]]. [[4:5|redeeming the time|Tempus redimentes]], that is, spending it fruitfully.

paras.t: Sermo vester semper in gratia, id est per gratiam Dei, sale sit conditus, id est sapientiali discretione temperatus. Sermo enim opportunus optimus est, teste Scriptura. Porro per sal, sapientia seu discretio designatur. Nam sicut sal est condimentum ciborum, ita discretio est condimentum verborum operumque bonorum. Propter quod in Levitico jubetur : In omni sacrificio offeres sal. Apostolis quoque dicitur : Vos estis sal terræ. Et iterum præcepit Christus : Habete in vobis sal. Ut sciatis quomodo, id est quam diversimode, quando, quo fine, ubi, quantum et qualiter, oporteat vos unicuique, id est omnibus interrogantibus, respondere, aliter scilicet docto, aliter indocto, aliter fideli, aliter infideli. In Proverbiis enim scriptum est : Responsio mollis frangit iram, sermo durus suscitat furorem. Hinc Petrus in prima sua Canonica ait : Parati semper ad satisfactionem omni poscenti vos rationem de ea quæ in vobis est fide et spe.
paras.en: [[4:6|Let your speech be always in grace|Sermo vester semper in gratia]], that is, through the grace of God, [[4:6|seasoned with salt|sale sit conditus]], that is, tempered with wise discretion. For [[Prov 15:23|a word in due time is best|Sermo enim opportunus optimus est]], as Scripture testifies. Now by salt is signified wisdom or discretion. For as salt is the seasoning of food, so discretion is the seasoning of good words and works. For which reason it is commanded in Leviticus: [[Lev 2:13|In all thy oblations thou shalt offer salt|In omni sacrificio offeres sal]]. To the Apostles also it is said: [[Matt 5:13|You are the salt of the earth|Vos estis sal terræ]]. And again Christ commanded: [[Mark 9:49|Have salt in you|Habete in vobis sal]]. [[4:6|that you may know how|Ut sciatis quomodo]], that is, in how many different ways, when, for what end, where, how much and in what manner, [[4:6|you ought to answer every man|oporteat vos unicuique respondere]], that is, all who question you: namely, one way to the learned, another to the unlearned, one way to the believer, another to the unbeliever. For it is written in Proverbs: [[Prov 15:1|A mild answer breaketh wrath: but a harsh word stirreth up fury|Responsio mollis frangit iram, sermo durus suscitat furorem]]. Hence Peter says in his first Canonical epistle: [[1 Pet 3:15|being ready always to satisfy every one that asketh you a reason of that hope which is in you|Parati semper ad satisfactionem omni poscenti vos rationem de ea quæ in vobis est]], in faith and hope.

paras.t: Quæ circa me sunt, id est statum meum et adversa quæ patior, omnia vobis proprio ore nota faciet Tychicus lator hujus epistolæ, carissimus frater noster, et fidelis minister Christi in prædicando, et conservus noster in Domino. Quem misi ad vos in hoc ipsum, id est propter hanc causam; et etiam ut cognoscat quæ circa vos sunt, id est statum vestrum, et consoletur corda vestra, verbis benignis inducendo vos ad patientiam, commemorando quoque æterna futuraque gaudia vobis parata, instruendo etiam non esse servanda cærimonialia legis Mosaicæ. Misi, inquam, cum Onesimo carissimo, et fideli fratre nostro spirituali, qui est ex vobis oriundus. Erat autem servus Philemonis civis Colossensis, sicut patebit plenius in epistola ad Philemonem. Qui Tychicus atque Onesimus omnia quæ hic in Epheso aguntur, nota facient vobis. Cum his duobus misit Apostolus præsentem epistolam, propter majorem Colossensium certificationem, ut scirent epistolam vere ab Apostolo missam.
paras.en: [[4:7|All the things that concern me|Quæ circa me sunt]], that is, my state and the adversities I suffer, [[4:7|Tychicus|Tychicus]], the bearer of this epistle, will by word of mouth [[4:7|make known to you|omnia vobis proprio ore nota faciet]]: [[4:7|our dearest brother|carissimus frater]], [[4:7|and faithful minister|et fidelis minister]] of Christ in preaching, [[4:7|and fellow servant in the Lord|et conservus noster in Domino]]. [[4:8|What I have sent to you for this same purpose|Quem misi ad vos in hoc ipsum]] [the Douay-Rheims prints “What”, a misprint for “Whom”], that is, for this cause; and also [[4:8|that he may know the things that concern you|ut cognoscat quæ circa vos sunt]], that is, your state, [[4:8|and comfort your hearts|et consoletur corda vestra]], leading you to patience with kind words, recalling to you also the eternal joys to come that are prepared for you, and teaching you too that the ceremonies of the Mosaic law are not to be kept. I have sent him, I say, [[4:9|With Onesimus, a most beloved and faithful brother|cum Onesimo carissimo, et fideli fratre]], our spiritual brother, [[4:9|who is one of you|qui est ex vobis]], that is, born among you. He was the slave of Philemon, a citizen of Colossæ, as will appear more fully in the epistle to Philemon[[Philem 1:10||]]. Tychicus and Onesimus [[4:9|All things that are done here, they shall make known to you|omnia quæ hic in Epheso aguntur, nota facient vobis]], that is, all things done here at Ephesus. With these two the Apostle sent the present epistle, for the greater assurance of the Colossians, so that they might know that the epistle was truly sent by the Apostle.

paras.t: Salutat vos Aristarchus concaptivus meus, id est mecum captus, et Marcus, qui alio nomine dicebatur Joannes, consobrinus Barnabæ apostoli : erant enim filii sororum. De quo Marco accepistis materialiter mandata a me, vel alio quodam magno efficienter, ita quod mandavimus vobis non recipiendum esse a vobis hunc Marcum, eo quod orta tribulatione discessisset a me, rediens Jerusalem : ut in Actibus legitur. Si venerit jam vel postea Marcus iste ad vos, excipite illum. Rediit enim ad me, et reconciliatus est mihi. Salutat præterea vos et Jesus, qui dicitur justus. Qui sunt ex circumcisione, id est natione Judæi, qui sua salutatione attestantur veritati hujus epistolæ. Ideo certi sitis legalia non esse servanda. Hi soli, quoad Judæos conversos, sunt adjutores mei, evangelizando in regno Dei, id est in Ecclesia militanti seu cœtu fidelium. De quo regno ait Dominus in Evangelio : Simile est regnum cœlorum sagenæ missæ in mare, et ex omni genere piscium congreganti; itemque, Mittet Filius hominis angelos suos, et colligent de regno ejus omnia scandala. Qui mihi fuerunt solatio, fideliter adsistendo, et fortiter laborando.
paras.en: [[4:10|Aristarchus, my fellow prisoner, saluteth you|Salutat vos Aristarchus concaptivus meus]], that is, taken captive with me; [[4:10|and Mark|et Marcus]], who was called by another name John[[Acts 12:12||]][[Acts 12:25||]], [[4:10|the cousin german of Barnabas|consobrinus Barnabæ]] the apostle: for they were the sons of sisters. [[4:10|touching whom you have received commandments|De quo … accepistis … mandata]]: concerning this Mark you have received commands materially from me, or effectively from some other great person [[the Latin “materialiter … efficienter” is obscure as printed; the sense seems to be that the command came from Paul or through some other notable person]], namely that we commanded you that this Mark was not to be received by you, because when tribulation arose he had departed from me and returned to Jerusalem, as we read in the Acts[[Acts 13:13||]][[Acts 15:38||]][[Acts 15:39||]]. [[4:10|If he come unto you, receive him|si venerit ad vos, excipite illum]]: if this Mark should come to you, now or later, receive him. For he has come back to me and has been reconciled to me. Moreover there salutes you [[4:11|And Jesus that is called Justus|et Jesus, qui dicitur justus]]. [[4:11|who are of the circumcision|Qui sunt ex circumcisione]], that is, Jews by nation, who by their greeting bear witness to the truth of this epistle. Therefore be sure that the legal observances are not to be kept. [[4:11|These only|Hi soli]], as regards the converted Jews, [[4:11|are my helpers|sunt adjutores mei]] in preaching the gospel [[4:11|in the kingdom of God|in regno Dei]], that is, in the Church militant or the company of the faithful. Of this kingdom the Lord says in the Gospel: [[Matt 13:47|the kingdom of heaven is like to a net cast into the sea, and gathering together of all kinds of fishes|Simile est regnum cœlorum sagenæ missæ in mare, et ex omni genere piscium congreganti]]; and likewise, [[Matt 13:41|The Son of man shall send his angels, and they shall gather out of his kingdom all scandals|Mittet Filius hominis angelos suos, et colligent de regno ejus omnia scandala]]. [[4:11|who have been a comfort to me|Qui mihi fuerunt solatio]], by faithfully standing by me and labouring bravely.

paras.t: Salutat vos Epaphras, qui ex vobis est, id est natione Colossensis, servus Christi Jesu, semper sollicitus pro vobis in orationibus quas facit pro vestra salute, ut stetis perfecti et pleni in omni voluntate Dei, id est, perfecti ac integri sitis in exsecutione omnium præceptorum aut consiliorum Dei. Testimonium enim illi Epaphræ perhibeo, quod habet multum laborem pro vobis, orando, et me sollicitando ad scribendum. Hic enim est Epaphras de quo in exordio hujus epistolæ dictum est, quod prædicationem Archippi confirmaverat. Et pro his qui sunt Laodiciæ et qui Hierapoli, id est, etiam pro Laodicensibus ac Hierapolitanis plurimum sollicitatur, timens ne a pseudoapostolis fallantur. Salutat vos Lucas medicus carissimus, id est Lucas evangelista : qui artis medicæ erat : animarum tamen magis quam corporum medicus fuit; et Demas.
paras.en: [[4:12|Epaphras saluteth you, who is one of you|Salutat vos Epaphras, qui ex vobis est]], that is, a Colossian by nation, [[4:12|a servant of Christ Jesus, who is always solicitous for you in prayers|servus Christi Jesu, semper sollicitus pro vobis in orationibus]] which he makes for your salvation, [[4:12|that you may stand perfect and full in all the will of God|ut stetis perfecti et pleni in omni voluntate Dei]], that is, that you may be perfect and whole in carrying out all the precepts or counsels of God. [[4:13|For I bear him testimony that he hath much labour for you|Testimonium enim illi Epaphræ perhibeo, quod habet multum laborem pro vobis]], by praying and by urging me to write. For this is the Epaphras of whom it was said at the beginning of this epistle[[Col 1:7||]] that he had confirmed the preaching of Archippus [[the passage cited, Col 1:7, speaks of Epaphras as the one from whom they learned the faith; Archippus is not named there]]. [[4:13|and for them that are at Laodicea and them at Hierapolis|et pro iis qui sunt Laodiciæ, et qui Hierapoli]], that is, he is greatly concerned for the Laodiceans and the Hierapolitans too, fearing lest they be deceived by false apostles. [[4:14|Luke, the most dear physician, saluteth you|Salutat vos Lucas, medicus carissimus]], that is, Luke the evangelist, who was of the medical art, yet was a physician of souls more than of bodies; [[4:14|and Demas|et Demas]].

paras.t: Salutate ex parte nostra fratres qui sunt Laodiciæ, id est in urbe illa vestræ civitati vicina, et Nympham, mulierem devotam, prædicantium hospitatricem atque altricem, et quæ in domo ejus est ecclesiam, id est fidelem ejus familiam. Et quum lecta fuerit apud vos, id est in vestro conventu, epistola hæc, facite ut et in Laodicensium Ecclesia legatur : eisdem enim informationibus indigent quibus et vos, quum sint a pseudoapostolis præventi; et quoniam vobis vicini familiaresque sunt. Et eam quæ Laodicensium est, id est epistolam illis a me missam, vos legatis, ut mutuo proficiatis. Hæc autem epistola Laodicensium non est reservata in canone Scripturarum, neque in numero epistolarum Pauli : sicut nec prima trium epistolarum missarum Corinthiis, quemadmodum dictum est alio loco.
paras.en: [[4:15|Salute the brethren who are at Laodicea|Salutate fratres, qui sunt Laodiciæ]] on our behalf, that is, in that city neighbouring your own; [[4:15|and Nymphas|et Nympham]], a devout woman [[Denis takes the name as feminine, Nympha]], the hostess and nourisher of the preachers, [[4:15|and the church that is in his house|et quæ in domo ejus est, ecclesiam]], that is, her faithful household. [[4:16|And when this epistle shall have been read with you|Et cum lecta fuerit apud vos epistola hæc]], that is, in your assembly, [[4:16|cause that it be read also in the church of the Laodiceans|facite ut et in Laodicensium ecclesia legatur]]: for they need the same instruction as you, since they have been forestalled by false apostles, and because they are your neighbours and friends. [[4:16|and that you read that which is of the Laodiceans|et eam, quæ Laodicensium est, vos legatis]], that is, the epistle sent by me to them, so that you may profit one another. This epistle of the Laodiceans, however, has not been preserved in the canon of the Scriptures, nor in the number of Paul's epistles; just as neither has the first of the three epistles sent to the Corinthians, as was said in another place[[1 Cor 5:9||]].

paras.t: Insuper monet Apostolus Colossenses, ut pastorem suum hortentur ad diligentem officii sui exsecutionem. Et dicite Archippo episcopo vestro : Vide ministerium tuum, id est, officium curæ pastoralis perpende intentius, quod accepisti in Domino, id est, quod tibi a Deo commissum est, ut illud impleas, gregem tibi commissum verbo et exemplis pascendo, atque in omnibus te habendo ut decet pastorem, Christi vicarium. Ex quo elucescit, quod subditi licite possint prælatos suos excitare, hortari et animare, humiliter tamen et modeste.
paras.en: Further, the Apostle admonishes the Colossians to exhort their pastor to the diligent performance of his office. [[4:17|And say to Archippus|Et dicite Archippo]], your bishop: [[4:17|Take heed to the ministry|Vide ministerium]] [Latin “ministerium tuum”, thy ministry], that is, weigh more attentively the office of pastoral care [[4:17|which thou hast received in the Lord|quod accepisti in Domino]], that is, which has been committed to thee by God, [[4:17|that thou fulfil it|ut illud impleas]], feeding the flock committed to thee by word and example[[1 Pet 5:2||]], and bearing thyself in all things as befits a pastor, the vicar of Christ. From this it shines out that subjects may lawfully rouse, exhort and encourage their prelates, yet humbly and modestly.

paras.t: Salutatio mea quæ subditur, scripta est manu Pauli, id est, propria manu verba salutationis meæ hæc scripsi, ut sciatis epistolam missam a me, non a falsis : qui interdum sub nomine verorum Apostolorum fallaces miserunt epistolas, ut magis deciperent. Quidam dicunt totam epistolam hanc manu Apostoli scriptam, propter certificationem prædictam. Memores estote vinculorum meorum, id est, attendite cur ista sustineo, ut et vos similia pati sitis parati, et pro me oretis, vel necessaria ministrare curetis. Deinde salutatio ponitur. Gratia Domini nostri Jesu Christi sit vobiscum, id est in cordibus vestris. Ipse est enim creator vester atque salvator, Unigenitus Patris, super omnia Deus sublimis et benedictus. Amen.
paras.en: [[4:18|The salutation|Salutatio]], my own, which follows, is written [[4:18|of Paul with my own hand|mea manu Pauli]]: that is, I have written these words of my greeting with my own hand, so that you may know the epistle was sent by me and not by false men, who at times sent lying epistles under the name of the true Apostles, the better to deceive. Some say that this whole epistle was written by the Apostle's hand, for the assurance just mentioned. [[4:18|Be mindful of my bands|Memores estote vinculorum meorum]], that is, consider why I endure these things, so that you too may be ready to suffer the like, and may pray for me, or take care to minister to me what I need. Then the greeting is set down. [[4:18|Grace|Gratia]] of our Lord Jesus Christ [[4:18|be with you|vobiscum]], that is, in your hearts. For He is your creator and saviour, the Only-begotten of the Father, God exalted above all and blessed. [[4:18|Amen|Amen]].
